The Most Favoured Nation principle under GATT provided that preferential trading agreements reached with one country should be extended to other countries.
The WTO has been able to cover in its agreements the agriculture and textile sectors which are the principal concerns for the Least Developed Countries (LDCs).
exp: General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) and World Trade Organisation(WTO): The General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) was signed by 23 countries in October 1947 after World War II and entered into force on January 1, 1948. The purpose of the GATT was to facilitate international trade. The GATT was held eight times in total from April 1947 to December 1993, each with great success and results. In 1995, the GATT was merged into the World Trade Organization (WTO) and the WTO was enlarged. All signatory members of the GATT should be treated equally with all other members. This is known as Most Favored Nation and has carried over to the WTO. The practical result of this is that when a country negotiates a tariff reduction with another country (usually a major trading partner), the same reduction automatically applies to all GATT signatories. The Agreement on Agriculture (AoA), a WTO treaty negotiated during the Uruguay Round of the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT), was formally ratified in 1994 in Marrakech, Morocco. It came into effect in 1995. Preferential Trade Agreement (PTA) term used in the WTO for preferential trade such as: reduced or zero tariffs that Member States can unilaterally offer to their trading partners. This includes the Generalized System of Preferences, under which developed countries grant preferential tariffs on imports from developing countries. | | Defence It includes non-reciprocal schemes granted by the General Council. Member States are therefore exempt from the application of the Most Favored Nation (MFN). Hence, the correct answer is option (C).

subject: economy
q: Under flexible exchange rate system, the exchange rate is determined:
o: As a weighted index of a group of currencies
exp: Key Points- Flexible exchange rate system is a type of exchange system where the exchange rate is predominantly on demand and supply of money in the market. Explanation- In a flexible exchange rate system, as per the changes in demand and supply of foreign exchange, the currency is allowed to fluctuate freely. There is no involvement of the central bank in this system and neither is there any need of maintaining foreign reserves. Appreciation and Depreciation of currency take place in this type of exchange system. Hence the correct option is Option A i.e. predominantly by market mechanism.

subject: economy
q: Which one of the following is an example of a 'natural monopoly'?
exp: Key Points- Delhi Jal Board is an example of natural monopoly and it is the most efficient provider in its industry. Explanation- Natural Monopoly is a type of monopoly where a single company is capable of providing a product or service at a cost which is lower as compared to its competitor in the industry. It arises due to natural market forces. Examples include industries related to electricity and water services. Hence the correct option is Option B i.e. Delhi Jal Board.

subject: economy
q: In view of the fact that kerosene is an inferior good in India, what is/are its implication(s)? 1. As households get richer, they consume less kerosene. 2. Over time there is a decline in quality of kerosene. 3. Government needs to stop subsidies on kerosene. Select the correct answer using the code given below.
exp: Key Points- Inferior goods refer to those type of goods whose demand decreases with increase in income of households. Explanation- Since kerosene is an inferior good, its demand will decrease with the rise of income of households. With the rise in income of households, they can afford other costlier alternatives in place of inferior goods. Thus, Statement 1 is correct. Statements 2 and 3 are incorrect as there is not necessarily a decline of quality of inferior goods after a period of time. Hence the correct answer is Option A i.e 1 only is the correct answer.

subject: geography
q: Majuli, the largest riverine Island is found in which of the following rivers?
exp: Majuli is a large riverine island located in the Brahmaputra River in the northeastern state of Assam, India. Here are some key points about Majuli: Geographical Location: Majuli is situated in the Brahmaputra River and is known for its unique geographical features. It lies in northeastern Assam and is part of the Jorhat district. Size and Significance: Majuli is recognized as the world's largest riverine island. It covers an area of around 880 square kilometres, although this size can fluctuate due to erosion and flooding. Hence, the correct answer is option C.

subject: geography
q: "Hippocamp" is Moon of which planet?
exp: Neptune is the solar system's eighth and farthest known planet from the sun. Hippocamp is the moon of Neptune. In Roman mythology, Neptune is known as the 'God of the sea'. Neptune has 14 known moons, including Hippocamp. Hippocamp was discovered on 1 July 2013 by astronomer Mark Showalter. Neptune has the longest orbital period, taking the maximum time for revolution around the sun. It has the longest year among all planets in the solar system. Neptune exhibits features like the Great Dark Spot, a large storm system similar to Jupiter's Great Red Spot. Hence, the correct answer is option B.

subject: geography
q: Which one of the following river passes through the largest freshwater lake of India?
exp: Wular Lake is the largest freshwater lake in India and one of the largest in Asia. It is situated in the Bandipora district in the Indian state of Jammu and Kashmir and is fed by the Jhelum River. Hence, the correct answer is option C.

subject: geography
q: Kalahari desert is located in which country?
exp: The Kalahari Desert is a large semi-arid sandy desert located in Southern Africa. Its name is derived from the Tswana word Kgala, which means "the great thirst", or Kgalagadi, meaning "a waterless place". During summer, temperatures in the Kalahari Desert can reach up to 45 degrees Celsius. Winter nights in the desert can see temperatures drop to as low as minus 15 degrees Celsius. The Kalahari Desert covers an area that spans Botswana, the eastern third of Namibia, and the northernmost part of the Northern Cape Province in South Africa. Hence, the correct answer is option A.

subject: geography
q: The Keibul Lamjao National Park is located in which of the following states?
exp: The Keibul Lamjao National Park is located in the state of Manipur. It is situated in the Bishnupur district, about 53 kilometers from Imphal. The Keibul Lamjao National Park is the world's only floating national park. It is located on the Loktak Lake, which is the largest freshwater lake in Northeast India. The park is known for its phumdis, which are floating masses of vegetation, soil, and organic matter. The park was established in 1977 and is managed by the Government of India. It is home to the endangered brow- antlered deer, also known as the Sangai or dancing deer. Hence, the correct answer is option (B).

subject: english
q: Read the sentence to find out whether there is any error in it or not. The error, if any, will be in one part of the sentence. The number of that part (which has the error) is the answer. If there is no error, the answer is (4). Ignore errors of punctuation, if any. The more you (1)/ work hard, (2)/ the more better you get (3)./ No error (4)
exp: The error is in part (3) of the sentence. the more better you get (3): This is incorrect. "Better" is already a comparative adjective. Using "more" before it creates a double comparative, which is not grammatically correct. Therefore, the answer is C. the more better you get. The corrected sentence should be: The more you work hard, the better you get.

subject: english
q: Fill in the blank with a suitable phrase preposition. I will introduce you ______ my boss this week.
exp: The best option to introduce someone is: B. to On - The word on is used to refer to something that is touching the surface of something else. To is the most common preposition used to indicate the recipient of an introduction. "I will introduce you to my boss" means you'll be presented to your boss for the first time. Too is an adverb used for emphasis or comparison, not for introductions. For - We use for to talk about a purpose or a reason for something Therefore, "I will introduce you to my boss this week" is the grammatically correct and natural way to express this.

subject: history
q: Red fort was built during the reign of which of the following rulers?
exp: The Red Fort, also known as Lal Qila, was constructed during the reign of Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan. The construction of the Red Fort began in 1638 and was completed in 1648. Shah Jahan commissioned the fort as part of his new capital, Shahjahanabad, the seventh city of Delhi. The Red Fort is renowned for its stunning Mughal architecture, which combines Persian, Timurid, and Indian styles. The fort's most distinctive feature is its red sandstone walls, which give it the name "Red Fort." Hence, the correct answer is option C.

subject: history
q: Which among the following was not the Navratna of the Akbar's court?
exp: The Navratnas, or "nine gems," were a group of nine extraordinary people in the court of Emperor Akbar, known for their outstanding contributions in various fields. The correct answer to the question of who among the following was not one of the Navratnas in Akbar's court is Bairam Khan Bairam Khan was a prominent military commander and regent during Akbar's early years but was not part of the group known as the Navratnas. Hence, the correct answer is option D.

subject: history
q: Which of the following Veda mentions about magical rituals and charms?
exp: The Atharva Veda is one of the four Vedas and mentions magical rituals and charms. It is sometimes called the "Veda of magical formulas," although some scholars dispute this epithet. The Samhita layer of the Atharva Veda reflects a tradition dating back to the 2nd millennium BCE. This tradition includes magico-religious rites to address superstitious anxieties, spells to alleviate ailments believed to be caused by demons, and herbal and nature-based potions used as medicine. The Vedas are a collection of Hindu and other ancient religious texts composed in ancient India between 1500 and 1000 BCE. The Rigveda is the oldest Vedas, containing hymns and prayers dedicated to various deities. Hence, the correct answer is option C.

subject: history
q: Which of the following revolutionary organizations was formed outside India?
exp: The Ghadar Party was an international political organization formed by expatriate Indians to overthrow British rule in India. Initially named the Pacific Coast Hindustan Association, it was founded on July 15, 1913, in San Francisco, United States, under the leadership of Lala Har Dayal, with Sohan Singh Bhakna as its president. The Ghadar Party gained significant support among Indian expatriates in the United States, Canada, East Africa, and Asia. The Ghadar Movement began to lose momentum as the British intensified their crackdown. By 1917, during the concluding years of World War I, the Ghadar Party split into Communist and Socialist factions. Hence, the correct answer is option B.

subject: history
q: The painting of Bodhisattva Padmapani is one of the most famous and oft-illustrated paintings at
exp: The Ajanta Caves, located in Maharashtra, India, are renowned for their ancient rock-cut Buddhist cave monuments and beautiful paintings. These caves, dating back to the 2nd century BCE to the 6th century CE, contain exquisite wall paintings and sculptures depicting various aspects of Buddhism, including the life of Buddha, Jataka tales, and Bodhisattvas like Padmapani. The painting of Bodhisattva Padmapani in Ajanta is particularly famous for its intricate details, vibrant colors, and religious significance, making it a subject of interest and admiration among art enthusiasts and historians. Hence, the correct answer is option (D).

subject: history
q: The Council of Ministers during the time of Shivaji Maharaj was known as:
exp: Ashta Pradhan was the council of ministers during the time of Shivaji Maharaj. This council consisted of eight prominent officials who assisted Shivaji in administering his empire. The Ashta Pradhan included positions such as the Peshwa (Prime Minister), Amatya (Finance Minister), Sachiv (Secretary), and Senapati (Commander-in-Chief), among others. Each member had specific responsibilities and played a crucial role in the governance and efficient functioning of Shivaji's administration. Hence, the correct answer is option (D).

subject: history
q: Who presided over 1907 Indian National Congress Session at Surat ?
exp: Ras Behari Ghosh presided over the 1907 Indian National Congress session at Surat. This session was notably marked by the split between the moderates and the extremists within the Congress. Mainly there was an ideological difference between the two groups. The main objectives placed by the extremist were: 1. Demand for the resolution of Swaraj. 2. Lala Lajpat Rai to be made the President of INC. These two demands were not accepted by the moderates thus initiated the split. The Surat Split was a victory of the British policy of Divide and Rule. In 1916, Lucknow session both the groups reunited again. Hence, the correct answer is option (C).

subject: history
q: Who was the founder of the Satyashodhak Samaj?
exp: Jyotiba Phule founded the Satyashodhak Samaj in Pune, Maharashtra. He established the organization in 1873 to promote social equality, education, and the upliftment of oppressed classes in India, challenging caste discrimination and advocating for the rights of marginalized communities. Hence, the correct answer is option (A).

subject: history
q: Who presided the 1905 Congress session?
exp: The Congress session in Banaras (1905) was presided by Gopal Krishan Gokhale. Indian National Congress Session President of the Session 1. Surat Session (1907) Dadabhai Naoroji 2. Calcutta Session (1906) Ras Behari Ghosh 3. Banaras Session (1905) Gopal Krishna Gokhale Hence, the correct answer is option (D).

subject: history
q: Which of the following pair is incorrectly matched?
o: Maulana Abul Kalam Azad - Al Hilal
exp: Bal Gangadhar Tilak, a prominent figure in the Indian independence movement, was associated with the Marathi newspaper Kesari. Jawaharlal Nehru, the first Prime Minister of independent India, was associated with Navjivan. Mahatma Gandhi was associated with Young India and Harijan, not National Herald. National Herald was associated with Jawaharlal Nehru and the Indian National Congress. Maulana Abul Kalam Azad, a prominent Indian freedom fighter, scholar, and the first Minister of Education in independent India, was associated with Al-Hilal. Hence, the correct answer is option (C).

subject: history
q: The First Battle of Panipat, which was fought in 1526, was between Babur and whom?
exp: The First Battle of Panipat was fought between Babur and Ibrahim Lodi. When: The battle took place on April 21, 1526. Where: The battle was fought near the village of Panipat, in present-day Haryana, India. Who won: Babur's forces defeated Ibrahim Lodi's army. Result: The Delhi Sultanate was overthrown and Babur became the Emperor of Delhi and Agra. How Babur won: Babur's forces used gunpowder firearms and cannons, and were aided by new artillery from the Ottoman Turks. Hence the correct answer is option (A).

subject: history
q: Which of the following Gupta rulers received the title "Kaviraja"?
exp: Samudragupta adopted the title of Kaviraja (King of poets). He was an expert ' Veena' player. Gupta King Samudragupta loved to play the flute and love poems. Renowned for his patronage of the arts and his own poetic talents, Samudragupta's reign marked a significant cultural and intellectual period in the Gupta Empire. Hence, the correct answer is option (C).

subject: history
q: Which Indian was removed from the Indian Civil Services (ICS) by the British?
exp: Surendranath Banerjee, one of the earliest Indians to join the Indian Civil Services, was removed from his position by the British in 1874. The removal was based on a procedural error concerning his age, which many considered an act of racial discrimination. Banerjee later became a prominent leader in the Indian independence movement. Hence, the correct answer is option (B).

subject: history
q: Who defeated the Marathas in the Third Battle of Panipat?
exp: The Third Battle of Panipat occurred on 14 January 1761 at Panipat, about 60 miles (95.5 km) north of Delhi. It was fought between a northern expeditionary force of the Maratha Empire and a coalition of the King of Afghanistan, Ahmad Shah Abdali, with two Indian Muslim allies—the Rohilla Afghans of the Doab and Shuja-ud-Daula, the Nawab of Oudh. The battle is considered one of the largest fought in the 18th century and has perhaps the largest number of fatalities in a single day reported in a classic formation battle between two armies. This battle resulted in the defeat of the Marathas. Hence, the correct answer is Option B.

subject: history
q: Adhai Din Ka Jhonpra in Ajmer was built by ______.
exp: Adhai Din Ka Jhonpra is a historical mosque in the city of Ajmer in Rajasthan, India. It is one of the oldest mosques in India, and the oldest surviving monument in Ajmer. Built by Qutb-ud-Din-Aibak in 1192 CE and designed by Abu Bakr of Herat, the mosque is an example of early Indo- Islamic architecture. The structure was completed in 1199 CE and was further enhanced by Iltutmish of Delhi in 1213 CE. The mosque retained most of the original Indian features, especially on the ornate pillars. The structure was used as a mosque up to 1947. Hence, the correct answer is Option A i.e Qutubuddin Aibak.

subject: history
q: Who founded the Mughal Empire in India?
exp: The Mughal Empire is conventionally said to have been founded in 1526 by Babur. He was a chieftain from what is today Uzbekistan, who employed aid from the neighbouring Safavid and Ottoman Empires, to defeat the Sultan of Delhi, Ibrahim Lodi, in the First Battle of Panipat, and to sweep down the plains of North India. He descended from the Turco-Mongol conqueror Timur on his father's side, and from Genghis Khan on his mother's side. He established himself in Kabul and then pushed steadily southward into India from Afghanistan through the Khyber Pass. Babur's forces defeated Ibrahim Lodi in the First Battle of Panipat in 1526. Hence, the correct answer is Option A i.e Babur.

subject: history
q: A contemporary rival dynasty of the Cholas in South India was ______.
exp: Vijayalaya, the successor of Srikantha Chola, founded the Chola empire. Vijayalaya belonged to Pottapi Chola family, a Telugu Chola branch that claimed descent from ancient Tamil king Karikala Chola and possibly a feudatory of the Pallava dynasty. Vijayalaya took an opportunity arising out of a conflict between the Pandya and Pallava empires in c. 850, captured Thanjavur from Muttarayar, and established the imperial line of the medieval Chola Dynasty. Thanjavur became the capital of the Imperial Chola empire. From the period of Rajaraja, the Cholas engaged in a series of conflicts with the Western Chalukyas. The Old Chalukya dynasty had split into two sibling dynasties, the Western and Eastern Chalukyas. Hence, the correct answer is Option C i.e Chalukyas of Kalyani.

subject: history
q: In which of the following regions Mahalwari system of Revenue Settlement was introduced?
exp: The Mahalwari system was used in India to protect village-level-autonomy. It was introduced by Holt Mackenzie in 1822. The word "Mahalwari" is derived from the Hindi word Mahal, which means a community made from a group of villages. Mahalwari consisted of landlords or Lambardars (also called as Nambardars) assigned to represent villages or groups of villages. Along with the village communities, the landlords were jointly responsible for the payment of taxes. Revenue was determined on basis of the produce of Mahal. Individual responsibility was not assigned. This system was prevalent in parts of the Gangetic Valley, Uttar Pradesh, the North Western province, parts of Central India and Punjab. The other two systems were the Permanent Settlement in Bengal in 1793 and the Ryotwari system in 1820. It covered the states of Punjab, Awadh and Agra, parts of Orissa, and Madhya Pradesh. Hence, the correct answer is Option D i.e North Western Provinces.

subject: history
q: Who was the first Governor-General of India?
exp: In 1835, Lord William Bentinck became the first governor general of India. The Governor-General of Indiawas the representative of the monarch of the United Kingdom in their capacity as the Emperor/Empress of India and after Indian independence in 1947, the representative of the Monarch of India. The office was created in 1773, with the title of Governor-General of the Presidency of Fort William. The officer had direct control only over his presidency but supervised other East India Company officials in India. Complete authority over all of British territory in the Indian subcontinent was granted in 1833, and the official came to be known as the "Governor-General of India". Hence, the correct answer is Option A i.e Lord William Bentrick.

subject: history
q: Who gave the title of "Sardar" to Vallabh Bhai Patel?
exp: Vallabhbhai Jhaverbhai Patel commonly known as Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, was an Indian independence nationalist and barrister who served as the first Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister of India from 1947 to 1950. Vallabhbhai Patel popularly known as Sardar Patel was an Indian politician who belonged to the Indian National Congress. Along with being a politician Sardar Patel was also an Indian Barrister and played an important role in India's struggle for independence. He also served as a home minister during the famous Indo-Pakistani war. It was women of bardoli who bestowed the title Sardar for the first time, which in Gujarati and most other Indian languages means Chief or Leader. Hence, the correct answer is Option C i.e Women of Bardoli.

subject: history
q: The famous revolt of 1857, of which Mangal Pandey was a part, is related to:
exp: Mangal Pandey was an Indian soldier whose attack on British officers on March 29, 1857, was the first major incident of what came to be known as the Indian, or Sepoy, Mutiny. Pandey was born in a town near Faizabad in what is now eastern Uttar Pradesh state in northern India, although some give his birth place as a small village near Lalitpur (in present-day southwestern Uttar Pradesh). He was from a high-caste Brahman landowning family that professed strong Hindu beliefs. Pandey joined the army of the British East India Company in 1849, some accounts suggesting that he was recruited by a brigade that marched past him. He was made a soldier (sepoy) in the 6th Company of the 34th Bengal Native Infantry, which included a large number of Brahmans. While he was posted at the garrison in Barrackpore in the mid-1850s, a new Enfield rifle was introduced into India that required a soldier to bite off the ends of greased cartridges in order to load the weapon. A rumour spread that the lubricant used was either cow or pig lard, which was repugnant to Hindus or Muslims, respectively The belief arose among the sepoys that the British had deliberately used the lard on the cartridges leading to the revolt of 1857. Hence, the correct answer is Option A i.e 34th Native Infantry.

subject: history
q: Who was the viceroy during the start of Non- cooperation movement?
exp: Lord Chelmsford served as Governor General and Viceroy of India from 1916 to 1921. Important events during his tenure included Lucknow Pact (1916), Khilafat Movement, Emergence of Gandhi as national leader, passing of Rowlatt Act and Jallianwalla Bagh Tragedy (1919), Non-Cooperation Movement, Third Afghan War and Treaty of Rawalpindi, August Declaration (1917), Montague- Chelmsford Reforms (1919). The Non-cooperation movement was a mass movement that involved participation from the nationalists as well as the public. The movement was to be nonviolent and to consist of Indians resigning their titles, boycotting government educational institutions, government service, foreign goods, and elections, and eventually, refusing to pay taxes. People resigned from their government jobs. People were asked to withdraw their children from government- controlled or aided schools and colleges. This movement was a great success as it got massive encouragement from millions of Indians. This movement almost shook the British authorities. Hence, the correct answer is Option B i.e Lord Chelmsford.

subject: polity
q: Consider the following statements: 1. The term of Prime Minister in five years. 2. The constitution provides that the President has to appoint the leader of the majority party in the Lok Sabha as Prime Minister. 3. Nominated members of the Rajya sabha cannot become the Prime Minister. Which of the statements given above is/are incorrect?
exp: The term of the Prime Minister is not fixed at five years; it is determined by the duration of the Lok Sabha. The President appoints the leader of the majority party in the Lok Sabha as Prime Minister, not necessarily the leader of the majority party. Additionally, nominated members of the Rajya Sabha can become the Prime Minister, as there is no constitutional bar against it. Hence, the correct answer is option (D).

subject: polity
q: Which Article of the Constitution deals with financial emergency?
exp: Article 360 of the Indian Constitution empowers the President to invoke financial emergency. Grounds of declaration – If the President is satisfied that a situation has arisen due to which the financial stability or credit of India or any part of its territory is threatened. Hence, the correct answer is option (C).

subject: polity
q: Which article is BR Ambedkar called "Heart and soul of the Constitution"?
exp: B.R. Ambedkar referred to Article 32 of the Indian Constitution as the "heart and soul of the Constitution." This article guarantees the right to constitutional remedies, which allows citizens to move the Supreme Court of India to seek enforcement of their fundamental rights. Ambedkar considered this provision crucial for upholding and protecting the fundamental rights of Indian citizens. Hence, the correct answer is option (A).

subject: polity
q: Anti-defection is present in which of the following schedule of the constitution?
exp: Anti-defection laws are enshrined in the 10th Schedule of the Indian Constitution. This schedule was added via the 52nd Amendment Act, 1985, to address the issue of political defections by legislators. It lays down the procedures for disqualification of members of Parliament and state legislatures on grounds of defection. The law prohibits elected members from defecting from their party without facing disqualification. This measure aims to promote stability and integrity in the political system by discouraging opportunistic party- switching. Hence, the correct answer is option (A).

subject: polity
q: What is the basic difference between Fundamental rights and DPSPs?
exp: Fundamental Rights are justiciable and enforceable, meaning citizens can approach courts if these rights are violated. They are considered sacrosanct and inviolable, providing individuals with legal protection. Directive Principles of State Policy are non-justiciable and not enforceable by courts. Hence, the correct answer is option (A).

subject: polity
q: Which of the statements given above is/are correct about Niti Ayog?
o: It is a public policy think tank body in India.
President is the chairperson of Niti Ayog.
exp: A. "It is a public policy think tank body in India." - This statement is correct. Niti Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) is indeed a public policy think tank body in India. B. "It is a constitutional body." - This statement is incorrect. Niti Aayog is not a constitutional body. It was formed by an executive order of the Government of India in 2015, replacing the erstwhile Planning Commission. C. "It was established in 2010." - This statement is incorrect. Niti Aayog was established on January 1, 2015, not in 2010. D. "President is the chairperson of Niti Ayog." - This statement is incorrect. The Prime Minister of India serves as the chairperson of Niti Aayog, not the President. Hence, the correct answer is option (A).

subject: polity
q: Who has the power to advise the president of India under Article 143?
exp: Under Article 143 of the Indian Constitution, the President of India has the power to seek the opinion of the Supreme Court of India on any question of law or fact that has arisen or is likely to arise and that, in the President's opinion, is of public importance. Therefore, it is the Supreme Court of India that advises the President under Article 143. Hence, the correct answer is option (A).

subject: polity
q: Which article of the Indian Constitution deals with the role and independence of the judiciary?
exp: The article of the Indian Constitution that deals with the role and independence of the judiciary is Article 124. Article 124 establishes the Supreme Court of India, outlining its composition and the appointment of judges, thus signifying the foundation for the judiciary's independence within the constitution. Key points about Article 124: Supreme Court establishment: It states that there shall be a Supreme Court of India. Chief Justice: The Supreme Court will consist of a Chief Justice of India and other judges as prescribed by Parliament. Appointment of Judges: The President appoints the judges of the Supreme Court. Tenure: Judges hold office until they reach the age of 65. Hence, the correct answer is option (A).

subject: polity
q: In which year was NITI Aayog formed?
exp: The National Institution for Transforming India (NITI Aayog) is a government think tank that advises the central and state governments on policy and development. The Aayog was formed in 2015 to promote cooperative federalism and the adoption of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Objectives Provide strategic advice to the government, Promote research and innovation, Develop a frameworbbbk for the national agenda, Foster collaborative federalism, and Develop mechanisms for formulating plans at the village level. | | Defence Initiatives: Vocal for Local: Promotes grassroots entrepreneurship and self-reliance Frontier Technology Labs: Established in schools by Atal Innovation Mission, NITI Aayog, and Meta National Conference to Accelerate Sustainable Development Goals: Spearheaded by NITI Aayog in partnership with the Government of Rajasthan, UNDP, and UN Governing Council: The Governing Council is made up of Chief Ministers of all the States and Union Territories with legislatures and Lt Governors of other Union Territories The Governing Council evolves a shared vision of national priorities and strategies Support: NITI Aayog is supported by the Development Monitoring and Evaluation Organisation (DMEO), Atal Innovation Mission (AIM), and National Institute of Labour Economics Research and Development (NILERD) Hence, the correct answer is option (B).

subject: polity
q: Who appoints the governors of Indian states?
exp: The Governor of a State is appointed by the President for a term of five years and holds office during his pleasure. Only Indian citizens above 35 years of age are eligible for appointment to this office. A governor acts as the constitutional head and takes all their decisions based on the advice of chief minister and their council of ministers. The primary function of the governor is to preserve, protect and defend the constitution and the law as incorporated in their oath of office under Article 159 of the Indian constitution in the administration of the state affairs. Hence, the correct answer is Option B i.e President.

subject: polity
q: When was the National Commission for women set up?
exp: The National Commission for Women was set up as statutory body in January 1992 under the National Commission for Women Act, 1990 to review the Constitutional and legal safeguards for women. The first head of the commission was Jayanti Patnaik. As of 24 February 2024, Rekha Sharma is the chairperson. The objective of the NCW is to represent the rights of women in India and to provide a voice for their issues and concerns. The subjects of their campaigns have included dowry, politics, religion, equal representation for women in jobs, and the exploitation of women for labour. They have also discussed police abuses against women. The commission regularly publishes a monthly newsletter, Rashtra Mahila, in both Hindi and English Hence, the correct answer is Option A i.e 1992.

subject: polity
q: Who among the following became the first speaker of Lok Sabha?
exp: The speaker of the Lok Sabha is the presiding officer and the highest authority of the Lok Sabha, the lower house of the Parliament of India. Serving for a term of five years, the speaker is chosen from sitting members of the Lok Sabha. The first Lok Sabha was constituted in 1952. Shri G.V. Mavalankar was the first Speaker of Lok Sabha (15 May 1952- 27 February 1956). Ganesh Mavlankar is considered as the father of Lok Sabha. He was popularly called 'Dada Saheb'. Hence, the correct answer is Option D i.e Ganesh Vasudev Mavalankar.

subject: polity
q: What is the full from of MP in Parliament?
exp: In India, the people of a constituency elect a Member of Parliament (MP) to represent them in the legislative body and advocate for their needs and concerns at the national level. As an MP in India, one is responsible for participating in law-making by proposing and passing bills, participating in debates and discussions, and scrutinizing government policies. Moreover, in the parliamentary committees, MP plays a crucial role in discussing important issues and making decisions. Furthermore, beyond the parliament, you are constantly working to improve the lives of your constituents by addressing their problems and striving for their development. In many countries with bicameral parliaments, the term “Member of Parliament” (MP) refers explicitly to lower house members. Hence, the correct answer is Option B i.e Member of Parliament.

subject: polity
q: Article 17 of the Indian constitution deals with
o: Protection of life and personal liberty

q: Each of the digits in the number 7148356 is arranged in ascending order from left to right. The position of how many digits will remain unchanged as compared to that in the original number?
exp: The original number is 7148356. To solve this, we first arrange the digits in ascending order: 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8. Now, let's compare the original number with the new arrangement: Original: 7, 1, 4, 8, 3, 5, 6 Sorted: 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 We'll check the positions: The first digit, 7, moves to the 6th position. The second digit, 1, moves to the 1st position. The third digit, 4, moves to the 3rd position (unchanged). The fourth digit, 8, moves to the 7th position. The fifth digit, 3, moves to the 2nd position. The sixth digit, 5, moves to the 4th position. The seventh digit, 6, moves to the 5th position. Thus, the digit that remains in the same position is 4. So, the number of digits, the position of which remains unchanged in position is one. Hence, one is the correct answer.

subject: polity
q: Right to Information Act ______ mandates a timely response to citizen requests for government information.
exp: The Right to Information (RTI) Act was enacted by the Parliament of India in 2005. It gives citizens the legal right to access information held by public authorities, promoting transparency and accountability in governance. The Act mandates that government officials must respond in a time-bound manner (usually within 30 days) to RTI applications filed by citizens. It has been a key tool in exposing corruption, improving public services, and empowering citizens to participate in democracy. Hence, the correct answer is "2005".

subject: gk
q: The Champaran Satyagraha took place in _____ .
exp: The Champaran Satyagraha was the first major Satyagraha movement launched by Mahatma Gandhi in India. The movement was launched in Champaran district of Bihar, where the indigo planters had been forcing the peasants to grow indigo on 3/20th of their land. The peasants were forced to do this even if the indigo crop failed. Gandhi went to Champaran in April 1917, and he met with the peasants and listened to their grievances. He then launched the Satyagraha movement, and he asked the peasants to refuse to grow indigo. The movement was successful, and the indigo planters were forced to give up their exploitative practices. Hence, the correct answer is "1917".

subject: reasoning
q: Satya's birthday falls on 15th August and Meena's birthday falls on 25th June. If Meena's birthday was on Wednesday, what was the day on Sathya's birthday in the same year?
exp: Given: Meena’s birthday: 25 June (Wednesday) Satya’s birthday: 15 August (same year) Step 1: Count days between 25 June and 15 August Remaining days in June = 30−25=5 days Days in July = 31 days Days in August up to 15th = 15 days Total days = 5+31+15=51 days Step 2: Find day shift 51÷7=7 weeks + 2 days So the day advances by 2 days Step 3: Move 2 days ahead from Wednesday Wednesday → Thursday → Friday Hence, friday is the correct answer.

subject: reasoning
q: Divit's birthday is on Friday 30th June. On what day of the week will be Samar's Birthday in the same year if Samar was born on 15th November?
exp: Days left in June = 30 – 30 = 0 Days in November to count = 15 Thus, total number of days from Divit's birthday to Samar’s birthday = 31 + 31 + 30 + 31 + 15 = 138 Thus, number of odd days = 138 | 7 = 5 ...........(applying Modulo function which gives the remainder of the division. This is used here to separate the number of odd days from the number of weeks.) As Divit's birthday is on Friday, Samar’s birthday will on Friday + 5 days = Wednesday. Hence, Wednesday is the correct answer.

subject: reasoning
q: Aarav's birthday is on Sunday, 12 th March . On what day of the week will be Madhup's Birthday in the same year if Madhup was born on 10 th August?
exp: According to the question : Arav’s birthday is on 12th March, Sunday. We have to find that Mandhup’s b’day is on which day, if his birthday is on 10th August of the same year. The total number of days between 12 March and 10 August = (19 days left in March + number of days in April + number of days in May + number of days in June + Number of days in July + 10 days of August ) = ( 20 + 30 + 31 + 30 + 31 + 10 ) = 151 days A day repeats itself on the seventh day. Thus, number of weeks = 151 / 7 = 21 weeks + 4 days Since there are 21 complete weeks, but also 4 extra days. On the completion of 25 weeks, it was Sunday only. But 4 days after, ( counting from the day after Sunday ) 1.Monday 2.Tuesday 3.Wednesday 4.Thursday So , the day on 10th August will be Thursday. Hence , “ Thursday “ is the correct answer.

subject: polity
q: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution are related to citizenship?
exp: Part II of the constitution discuss the matters of citizenship of India under article 5-11. This part-II of constitution broadly classified the 4 categories only. The person who falls under categories might be the citizen of India from 26-01- 1950. 1. Person domicile in India 2. Persons who migrated from Pakistan 3. Persons who migrated to Pakistan 4. Person who is living abroad. Articles 15 to 21 of the Indian Constitution deal with fundamental rights. Articles 2 to 4 deal with the admission or establishment of new states and alteration of areas, boundaries, or names of existing states. Articles 25 to 31 pertain to fundamental rights related to freedom of religion, cultural and educational rights, and the right to property. Hence the correct answer is "Articles 5 to 11".

subject: computer
q: __________ changes each time it is installed to avoid detection by antivirus software.
exp: Some viruses are designed to change their code each time they spread. This change helps them avoid detection by antivirus software. Such viruses encrypt or modify their structure while keeping the same function. These characteristics describe a polymorphic virus. Hence, the correct answer is "Polymorphic virus".

subject: computer
q: A__________ is an agreement between the communicating parties on how communication is to proceed.
exp: In communication systems, certain rules must be followed for data exchange. These rules define how data is formatted, transmitted, and received. An agreement on communication procedures between parties is called a protocol. Other options do not define communication rules. Hence, the correct answer is "Protocol".

subject: computer
q: Which of the following is an application protocol?
exp: The Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) is an application protocol used for distributed, collaborative, and hypermedia information systems, serving as the foundation of data communication for the World Wide Web. HTTP (Hypertext Transfer Protocol) – Correct. It operates at the Application Layer (Layer 7 of the OSI model) and is used to load webpages and transfer hypermedia documents. TCP (Transmission Control Protocol) – Incorrect. It is a Transport Layer protocol responsible for reliable, ordered, and error-checked delivery of data. IP (Internet Protocol) – Incorrect. It is a Network Layer (Internet Layer) protocol responsible for addressing and routing packets across the internet. UDP (User Datagram Protocol) – Incorrect. It is a Transport Layer protocol used for fast, connectionless, and lightweight communication, often for streaming or DNS. Hence, the correct answer is "HTTP".

subject: computer
q: The complete form of 'IC' in electronics is
exp: In electronics, IC refers to a miniaturized electronic circuit. It contains multiple electronic components like transistors and resistors on a single chip. ICs are used in computers, mobile phones, and other electronic devices. The full form of IC is Integrated Circuit. Hence, the correct answer is "Integrated circuit".

subject: computer
q: What is the full form of 'LAN'?
exp: A LAN stands for Local Area Network. It consists of a series of computers linked together to form a network in a specific location. The computers in a LAN connect via IP ethernet or Wi-Fi. A LAN is normally exclusive to an organization, such as a school, association or office. LAN offers the following benefits: Resource sharing The relationship between the client and the server Internet sharing Sharing applications and software Data security Easy and fast communication Computer ID Hence, the correct answer is "Local Area Network".

subject: computer
q: The web uses __________ to request and serve web pages and programs.
exp: HTML stands for Hypertext Markup Language. It is the standard markup language for creating web applications and web pages. With CSS known as Cascading Style Sheets and JavaScript, HTML forms a triad of cornerstone technologies for the WWW (World Wide Web). Web browsers collect HTML documents from a web server or from local storage and deliver them into multimedia web pages. Hence, the correct answer is “Hyper Text Markup Language”.

subject: computer
q: In which graphics, digital photos and scanned images are typically stored with extensions such as.bmp, .png, .jpg, .tif or.gif?
exp: In Bitmap graphics, digital photos and scanned images are typically stored with extensions such as .bmp, .png, .jpg, tif or gif. Bitmap is a format in which an image is shown and stored digitally. It comprises various dots which together form the image. Such dots are called pixels, therefore as the number of dots in an image increases the clarity of the image increases. Hence the correct answer is “ Bitmap.”

subject: computer
q: Netscape Navigator is a ____.
exp: Netscape Navigator is a web browser that was discontinued in 2002 due to increased use of Microsoft’s Internet Explorer. Netscape Navigator was the flagship product of Netscape Communication Corp. In the 1990s it was the dominant web browser in terms of usage share. Graphical user interface is an interface that allows users to interact with different electronic devices using icons and other visual indicators. Computer programming language: It allows the user to give instructions to a computer in a language the computer understands. A processor is a unified electronic circuit that performs the calculations that run a computer. Hence, the correct answer is “web browser”.

subject: computer
q: ___________ is not a storage device.
exp: Linux is not a storage device; it is the best-known and most-used open-source operating system. As an operating system, Linux sits underneath all of the other software on a computer. It receives requests from programs and relays these requests to the computer's hardware. Linux is known for its stability, security, and flexibility. Hence, the correct answer is "Linux."

COUNT function is used to get the number of entries in a number field that is in a range or array of numbers SUM function is used to add multiple numeric values within different cells. Hence, the correct answer is “COUNTIF”.

q: Which of the following is not among the three different forms of 'if statement?
exp: if…and is not among the three different forms of 'if statement. If statement in Python is a very powerful decision-making statement used to control the flow of execution of statements. It is a two-way decision-making statement used with a relational or logical expression. It can be used in five ways: If else Nested if If else if ladder Simple if Single Line if Hence, the correct answer is “if…and”.

q: A cube is segmented into 5832 cubes. Before dividing the cube, each face of it is varnished with Blue colour. How many tiny cubes will be formed having more than 1 face coloured?
exp: Here, in the given question we have to find out the total number of tiny cubes that will be formed having two or three faces coloured. Total number of cubes having two faces coloured = (n - 2) × total number of edges in cube Total number of cubes having two faces coloured = (18 - 2) × 12 = 192 Total number of cubes having three faces coloured = Total number of corners in a cube Total number of cubes having three faces coloured = 8 So, the total number of cubes having more than one coloured = 192 + 8 = 200 Hence, 200 is the correct answer.
