subject: history
q: Abhinav Bharat Society was a secret society of revolutionaries. It was established in ___________.
exp: During the Bombay Presidency, the Abhinav Bharat Society was founded. In 1904, Vinayak Damodar Savarkar and his brother Ganesh Damodar Savarkar founded the Abhinav Bharat Society (Young India Society), a covert organization dedicated to Indian independence. It was originally called the "Mitra Mela" was held in Nasik when Vinayak Savarkar was still a student at Fergusson College in Pune. After then, the group grew to include several hundred political activists and revolutionaries, and Savarkar established branches not only in London, where he was studying law, but also in various other parts of India. The Abhinav Bharat Society carried out a few assassinations of British officials before the Savarkar brothers were found guilty and given prison sentences. The group was subsequently dissolved in 1952. Hence the correct answer is "Bombay Presidency"

subject: economy
q: The consumption of fixed capital is also known as _________.
exp: Consumption of fixed capital is also known as depreciation. Depreciation refers to the gradual decrease in the value of physical assets over time. It accounts for the cost of using and maintaining assets in the production process. Appreciation refers to the increase in the value of an asset or currency over time, typically due to factors such as market demand, economic conditions, or improved performance. Gross investment refers to the total spending on acquiring new capital goods, including replacements and additions, within an economy over a specific period. Hence the correct answer is "depreciation".

subject: economy
q: One of the following is also called as World Bank.
exp: The term “World Bank” refers to a group of international financial institutions that provide loans and grants for development. Its main lending institution is the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD), established in 1944. The World Bank today consists of IBRD + IDA (International Development Association), but the IBRD is most directly identified as the "World Bank." Other options: IMF (International Monetary Fund) → Manages global monetary cooperation and exchange rates. WTO (World Trade Organization) → Regulates global trade. IDA → Concessional lending arm of the World Bank Group, but not itself called “World Bank.” Hence, the correct answer is "IBRD".

subject: economy
q: What will you call a system of taxation under which the poorer sections are taxed at higher rates than the richer sections?
exp: In a regressive tax system, poorer sections bear a higher tax burden compared to richer sections. The tax rate decreases as income increases, so the poor pay a larger share of their income. Example: Indirect taxes like GST or sales tax affect low-income groups more. This is opposite to a progressive tax, where the rich are taxed at higher rates.

subject: economy
q: Which one of the following is not an instrument of Fiscal policy?
exp: Fiscal policy uses tools like taxation, public expenditure, and public borrowing to influence the economy. Open Market Operations (OMO) are a monetary policy tool used by the RBI to control money supply and interest rates, not part of fiscal policy. So, while taxation, borrowing, and expenditure are fiscal instruments, OMO is not.

subject: economy
q: What is the name of portal launched by RBI recently to check illegal money collection?
exp: RBI launched the Sachet portal to check illegal money collection activities. It allows people to lodge complaints against unauthorised deposit schemes. The portal provides details of entities allowed to accept deposits. It promotes awareness and protection for depositors against fraud.

subject: economy
q: When the demand for a good increases with an increase in income, such a good is called
exp: Normal Good → Demand increases when income increases. Inferior Good → Demand decreases when income increases (people shift to better alternatives). Superior Good (Luxury) → High-quality goods, demand rises more than proportionally with income. Giffen Good → Special case of inferior goods where demand increases even when price rises (rare). Hence, the correct answer is "Normal Good".

subject: economy
q: Which of the following produces the most solid waste?
exp: Manufacturing generates the most solid waste, especially in industrialized regions. This includes by-products, scrap materials, packaging waste, and chemical residues. Industries such as mining, metal production, and chemical manufacturing contribute heavily to this waste. Proper waste management and recycling are critical in minimizing environmental impacts. Hence, the correct answer is C) Manufacturing.

subject: economy
q: The term 'Macro Economics' was used by __________ .
exp: Macro Economics studies the economy as a whole (total output, employment, inflation). The term was first used by Ragnar Frisch in 1933. It is different from Micro Economics, which studies individual units like households and firms. Key focus areas include GDP, national income, unemployment, and inflation.

subject: economy
q: Disguised unemployment in India is mainly related to?
exp: Disguised unemployment means extra people are employed than actually required, so their removal doesn’t affect total output. In India, it is mainly found in the agricultural sector, especially in rural areas. Example: 5 people working on a farm where 3 can produce the same output, the extra 2 are disguisedly unemployed. It shows underemployment, not complete joblessness. Hence, the correct answer is “Agricultural sector”.

subject: economy
q: What situation would result if Government expenditure exceeds the Government revenue on Current Account?
exp: Government expenditure > Government revenue on current account means spending is higher than income. This gap between income and expenditure creates a shortfall. Such a shortfall in the budget is termed as a deficit. Hence, the correct answer is "Deficit budgeting".

subject: economy
q: IMF has predicted that the global economy would grow at _______% in 2017.
exp: In April 2017, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) released a report. According to the report, IMF anticipated the global economy to expand by 3.5%. This projection was based on various economic indicators and trends analyzed by IMF experts. The forecast suggested moderate growth for the global economy amidst prevailing economic conditions. Factors such as trade dynamics, monetary policies, and geopolitical events were considered in making this prediction. IMF's forecast served as a reference point for policymakers, businesses, and investors worldwide. Hence, the correct answer is "3.5."

subject: economy
q: Who gave the 'General Equilibrium Theory'?
exp: ‘General Equilibrium Theory’ was formulated by Leon Walras. It is also known as Walrasian Theory. He discussed General Equilibrium Theory in his book ‘ Elements of Pure Economics’. It describes the workings of the macroeconomy as a whole in place of assets of individual market anomalies. It also explains that the interaction of demand and supply results in an overall general equilibrium. This theory assumes a gap between actual and equilibrium prices. Adam Smith is known as the Father of Economics. and he is famous for his book ‘Wealth of Nations’. Hence, the correct answer is “Leon Walras”.

subject: economy
q: The ________ exchange rate is the relative price of foreign goods in terms of domestic goods.
exp: Real exchange rate is the ratio of price level abroad and domestic price level where foreign price level gets converted into domestic currency units through the current nominal exchange rate. It is the ratio of the foreign price level and domestic price level multiplied by the nominal exchange rate. Nominal exchange rate is the price of foreign currency in terms of the domestic currency. Fixed exchange rate is also known as a pegged exchange rate in which the value of a currency is fixed against the value of another currency. Hence, the correct answer is “Real”.

subject: economy
q: Union Cabinet approves amendments in M- SIPS to attract investment in electronics manufacturing. What is the full form of M- SIPS?
exp: The M-SIPS stands for Modified Special Incentive Package Scheme. It's a government initiative aimed at attracting investments in the electronics manufacturing sector. The scheme provides financial incentives to offset disabilities faced by electronics manufacturing companies in India. These incentives are designed to promote the growth of the domestic electronics manufacturing ecosystem. The Union Cabinet's approval of amendments signifies a commitment to further enhancing investment attractiveness. The amendments are likely to streamline processes and make the scheme more responsive to industry needs. Hence, the correct answer is "Modified Special Incentive Package Scheme."

subject: economy
q: _____ says that the marginal product of a factor input initially rises with its employment level. But after reaching a certain level of employment, it starts falling
exp: The law of variable proportions explains that when one factor of production is increased while others are held constant, the marginal product of that variable factor will initially increase. However, as more of the variable factor is employed, there comes a point where the marginal product begins to decline. This occurs due to factors such as limited space, equipment, or other fixed resources that can't be easily expanded. The law illustrates the idea that there's an optimal level of input usage beyond which efficiency decreases. This phenomenon is crucial for understanding production decisions and resource allocation in the short run. Hence, the correct answer is "Law of variable proportions."

subject: economy
q: Which tax causes a burden on the poorer section of the society?
exp: Money is essential to run a government and manage its affairs. For this, the government imposes a variety of taxes on the earnings of individuals and businesses. There are two types of taxes - direct taxes and indirect taxes. Direct taxes are imposed on individuals and companies by the country's supreme tax body. These taxes are directly paid by those on whom it is imposed. For instance, taxpayers directly pay income tax, tax on assets, and gifts to the government. Indirect taxes are imposed on goods and services and their final burden falls on the consumers. That is why it causes a burden on the poorer section of society. For eg - It doesn't matter how much you earn, you have to pay the same amount of tax on toothpaste as the other ones. Hence, the correct answer is “Indirect tax”

subject: economy
q: The ________ balance is the sum of the balance of merchandise trade, services and net transfers received from the rest of the world.
exp: The current account reflects the balance of goods and services and net transfers received from the rest of the world. It includes transactions like the purchase of goods and machinery, as well as investments made. The capital account, on the other hand, includes capital transactions such as investments in assets. Together, the capital and current accounts constitute the Balance of Payments, which records a country's economic transactions with the rest of the world. Hence, the correct answer is "Current Account."

subject: economy
q: Which of the following is represented by 'The Lorenz Curve'?
exp: The Lorenz curve is a graphical tool used to represent the distribution of income or wealth within a population. It was created by Max O. Lorenz in 1905 to show economic inequality. The curve plots the cumulative percentage of total income received against the cumulative percentage of recipients, starting from the poorest to the richest. A perfectly equal income distribution would be represented by a 45-degree line, known as the line of equality. The more the Lorenz curve bows away from the line of equality, the greater the inequality. Hence, the correct answer is "Income Distribution."

subject: economy
q: Goods for which the quantity that a consumer chooses increases as the consumer's income increases and decreases as the income decreases are called?
exp: Normal goods are goods whose demand rises when consumer income increases. Conversely, their demand falls when consumer income decreases. Examples include clothing, electronics, and branded products. They are different from inferior goods, whose demand decreases as income rises. Hence, the correct answer is "Normal goods".

subject: economy
q: Which one of the following is a component of Food Security System?
exp: Buffer stock is a measure of the Food Security System. It is the central stock maintained by the Government of India to meet the demand for various purposes of food security, such as taking care of emergency situations. Emergency situations can be crop failure due to climate change or stabilization of prices by way of market intervention. Minimum Support Price (MSP) is the assured price at which food grains are procured from farmers by the central and state governments and their agencies, for the central pool of foodgrains. Fair Price Shop means a shop which has been licensed to distribute essential commodities , to the ration card holders under the Targeted Public Distribution System.The term is defined in Section 2(4) of National Food Security Act, 2013. Mid-day meal (MDM) is a wholesome freshly-cooked lunch served to children in government and government-aided schools in India. Hence, the correct answer is "Buffer Stock".

subject: economy
q: Citizen of which neighbouring country does not require a passport or visa to enter India?
exp: Citizens of Nepal can enter India without a passport or visa. They can use their driver’s license, voter’s ID card, or ration card as identity proof. Nepali citizens can stay and work in India indefinitely without the need for a visa. Similarly, Indians going to Nepal enjoy similar ease of travel. This relaxed border policy fosters strong cultural and economic ties between the two nations. Hence, the correct answer is "Nepal."

subject: economy
q: In April 2017, the G20 Digital Ministerial Meeting on Digital Economy was held in which country?
exp: The G20 Digital Ministerial Meeting on Digital Economy took place in Dusseldorf, Germany. Ministers representing the digital economy from G20 nations participated in the event. The meeting resulted in the adoption of a declaration titled ‘Shaping Digitalisation for an Interconnected World’. Discussions revolved around various aspects of digitalization and its impact on global interconnectedness. The event aimed to foster collaboration and strategic planning among G20 countries in the digital sphere. Hence, the correct answer is "Germany."

subject: economy
q: Movement along the supply curve is known as_______.
exp: The movement along the supply curve takes place when all the factors affecting supply remain constant and only the price changes. Hence, when the price increases supply contracts, and when the price decreases supply expands. A rise or fall in the price of the commodity alone causes a movement along the supply curve. A movement along a supply curve represents a change in quantity supplied. It is caused by a change in the price of goods. There is a direct relationship between price and quantity supplied. Hence, The correct answer is "Expansion and contraction of supply".

subject: economy
q: Medium-term loans are provided for a period of ______.
exp: The long-term loan can be cleared or repaid within a time limit of 20-30 years. Medium-term loans where settlements are made over a period between one and three years. The Short-term loan is basically for less than a year. Hence, the correct answer is “1 year to 3 years”.

subject: economy
q: Which one of the following is not an instrument of credit control in India?
exp: Instrument of credit control refers to the instruments that are introduced by the RBI to control the money supply. These can be classified into Quantitative and Qualified instruments. Quantitative instruments include Bank rate, Repo rate, Reverse Repo rate, CRR, SLR and Open Market Operations while Qualitative instruments include Margin requirement, Rationing of credit, Direct Action and Moral Suasion. Rationing of credit is introduced when the supply of credit is to be checked by the RBI, particularly for speculative activities. Direct action is adopted when commercial banks do not cooperate with the RBI in controlling credit. Open Market Operations refer to the purchase and sale of securities in the open market by the RBI on behalf of the government. Hence, the correct answer is “Variable cost reserve ratios”.

subject: economy
q: In a centrally planned economy, the ________ plans all the important activities in the economy.
exp: Centrally planned economy is a system in which the government makes economic decisions rather than the interaction between businesses and consumers. Government of a centrally planned economy decides when and where production and investment will be directed. This economy is also known as a command economy as prices are controlled by a centrally managed government. This economy is different from a market economy in which market decisions are taken by businesses and consumers. Hence, the correct answer is “Government”.

subject: economy
q: Which of the following is not true about a Demand Draft?
o: It may be dishonored for lack of funds.
It is issued by a bank.
exp: Demand Draft cannot be dishonored by the Bank for the lack of funds. This is because Demand Draft guarantees the amount of money for which it is pledged and that money is taken before the draft is issued. Demand draft is a negotiable instrument that is similar to a bill of exchange. Bank issues a demand draft to its client, directing another bank or its branch to pay a certain sum to a specific party. Hence, the correct answer is “It may be dishonored for lack of funds”.

subject: economy
q: When there is only one buyer and one seller of the product, it is called a ______ situation.
exp: A bilateral monopoly involves a single buyer (monopsony) and a single seller (monopoly) of a product. It's like a tug-of-war between the buyer and seller, each having significant market power. Think of a labor union, which monopolizes labor supply, negotiating with a monopsonist, a single large employer in a town. The dynamics involve intense bargaining power struggles due to the limited options available. The buyer and seller have considerable influence over the price and quantity of the product or service. This scenario often leads to complex negotiations and sometimes even to inefficient outcomes. Hence, the correct answer is "Bilateral monopoly."

subject: economy
q: _________says that if we keep increasing the employment of an input, with other inputs fixed, eventually a point will be reached after which the resulting addition to output (i.e., the marginal product of that input) will start falling.
exp: Law of diminishing marginal product says that while increasing one input and keeping other inputs at the same level may initially increase output, further increases in that input will have a limited effect, and eventually negative or no effect on the output. Law of variable proportions says that ‘ an increase in some inputs relative to other fixed inputs will in a given state of technology cause output resulting from same additions of extra inputs will become less. In the short-run scenario, any one of the factors which are associated with production is fixed. In the long run, factors associated with production as well as associated costs are variable in nature. Hence, the correct answer is “Law of diminishing marginal product”.

subject: economy
q: ______ is the set of all possible combinations of the two inputs that yield the same maximum possible level of output.
exp: An isoquant shows the possibilities of any two inputs that result in the same output level. A set of technically effective operations that produce the same result are expressed by an isoquant. It is a curve that depicts all conceivable resource combinations that can result in a specific level of output based on the substitutability of inputs. Hence the correct answer is "Isoquant".

subject: economy
q: Which of the following is not a component of monetary policy in India?
exp: Public Debt (Government Debt) is the debt owed by the government, whereas monetary policy is framed and implemented by the RBI. Monetary policy tools include Repo Rate, Moral Suasion, and Credit Rationing, which are directly controlled and employed by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). Public Debt does not fall within the ambit of RBI's monetary policy measures and is managed separately by the government. Public debt includes the total liabilities of the Union government that have to be paid from the Consolidated Fund of India, and it is a key indicator of the government's financial health. Almost a fourth of the government expenditure goes into interest payment, highlighting the significant impact of public debt on government finances. Hence, the correct answer is "Public Debt."

subject: economy
q: ..................of an input is defined as the change in output per unit of change in the input when all other inputs are held constant.
exp: Marginal product of input or factor of production is a change in output resulting from employing one more unit of a particular input. Example, change in output when a firm's labor is increased from five to six units, assuming that quantities of other inputs are kept constant. Hence, the correct answer is “Marginal product”.

subject: economy
q: The closest example of a centrally planned economy is the ____ for the major part of the 20th Century.
exp: The closest example of a centrally planned economy is the Soviet Union for the major part of the 20th Century. A centrally planned economy, also known as a command economy, is an economic system where a government body makes economic decisions regarding the production and distribution of goods. The economy of the Soviet Union was based on a system of state ownership of the means of production, collective farming, and industrial manufacturing. The main character of the command economy is centralized administrative planning. Hence the correct answer is “ Soviet Union.”

subject: economy
q: Who takes the decision regarding the savings and loan activities in a Self Help Group (SHG)?
exp: Self-help groups are informal groups of people who come together to address their common problems. While self-help might imply a focus on the individual, one important characteristic of self-help groups is the idea of mutual support – people helping each other. . The Reserve Bank of India(RBI) was established following the Reserve Bank of India Act of 1934. It was nationalized in 1949. It is the central bank of India. A nongovernmental organization (NGO) is an organization independent of the government whose primary mission is not commercial and that focuses on social, cultural, environmental, educational, and other issues. Private sector banks are those whose stock is primarily owned by private companies or individuals. Hence, the correct answer is “Members of group”.

subject: reasoning
q: From the given words, select the word which cannot be formed using the letters of the given word. SMOTHERS
exp: Here, in this question we have to find the word which cannot be formed using the letters in the given word. Logic used here is that the given word must include the letters of the word. Given: SMOTHERS THOSE = SMOTHERS- (THOSE) - It can be formed as all letters are present in the given word. METRO = SMOTHERS - (METRO) - It can be formed as all letters are present in the given word. STORE = SMOTHERS - (STORE) - It can be formed as all letters are present in the given word. TEARS = SOMTHERS - (TEARS) - It cannot be formed as letter ‘A’ is not present in the given word. Hence, TEARS is the correct answer.

subject: economy
q: Which of the following organisations of the Government of India has been reporting the GDP at factor cost and at market prices?
exp: The market prices have been reported by the Central Statistics Office (CSO) of the Government of India. In 2015, CSO abandoned the method of calculating GDP based on factor costs and switched to using the worldwide standard of computing GDP based on market prices together with the Gross Value Added (GVA) measure in order to more accurately estimate economic activity. Hence the correct answer is Option C: Central Statistics Office.

subject: polity
q: Which was the first country to incorporate Fundamental Duties in its Constitution?
exp: The concept of incorporating Fundamental Duties in a constitution was pioneered by the USSR (Union of Soviet Socialist Republics). This marked a significant step in recognizing the responsibilities of citizens towards their nation and society. The inclusion of Fundamental Duties in a country's constitution emphasizes the importance of civic responsibilities alongside individual rights. The idea of Fundamental Duties later influenced various other countries, including India, to include similar provisions in their constitutions. Hence, the correct answer is "USSR".

subject: aptitude
q: In finding the HCF of two numbers by division method, the last divisor is 17 and the quotients are 1,11 and 2 , respectively. What is sum of the two numbers?
exp: As we know, Divided = Divisor × quotient + remainder Divided = 17 × 2 + 0 Divided = 34 Again, Divided = Divisor × quotient + remainder Divided = 34 × 11 + 17 Divided = 374 + 17 = 391 Again, Divided = Divisor × quotient + remainder Divided = 391 × 1 + 34 Divided = 391 + 34 = 425 The two numbers are 425 and 391 Sum of two numbers = 425 + 391 = 816 Hence, Option B is the correct answer.

subject: english
q: Select the sentence containing the homonym of the highlighted word: The medieval oriel window projected elegantly from the chapel wall.
o: The priest admired the sunlight filtering through the oriel.
The duke stood by the oriel gazing at the courtyard.
The technician adjusted the frequency on the aerial.
The stained-glass oriel was restored by artisans.
exp: The Correct Answer: Option C — The technician adjusted the frequency on the aerial. Explanation: "Aerial" is a homonym of "oriel." Homonyms are words that sound the same (or very similar) when spoken but have different meanings and spellings (also called homophones when they sound identical). "Oriel" (pronounced OR-ee-ul) refers to a type of projecting window, particularly in medieval architecture, while "aerial" (pronounced AIR-ee-ul) refers to an antenna used for transmitting or receiving radio/TV signals, or can mean "relating to the air." These words sound very similar in pronunciation, making them homonyms, despite their completely different meanings and spellings. Additional Info: Homonyms are words that sound alike but have different meanings: Homophones: sound the same, spelled differently (their/there/they're, to/too/two) Homographs: spelled the same, different meanings (bow: weapon vs. bow: bend forward) "Oriel" and "aerial" are homophones (sound similar/same, different spellings and meanings) Oriel: (noun) a bay window that projects from an upper floor, supported by brackets or corbels, common in medieval and Gothic architecture Aerial: (noun) an antenna for radio/TV signals; (adjective) relating to the air, occurring in the air Other examples of homophones: Knight/night, write/right, flour/flower, piece/peace, brake/break Pronunciation note: While "oriel" and "aerial" are very similar in sound, the exact pronunciation may vary by accent, but they are close enough to be considered homonyms/homophones.

subject: history
chapter: Important Committees and Commissions in British Times
q: Which of the following commissions recommended that "the appointment of Governor should be non-partisan"?
exp: In 1983, the government of India appointed members of the Sarkaria Commission to investigate the relationship and distribution of power between the central government and the various state governments. It was advised that persons with extensive years of experience in public service and non-partisan attitudes be appointed to the position of Governor during the process of selecting a candidate for the position of Governor. Hence, the correct answer is "Sarkaria Commission"

subject: gk
q: According to census 2011 , which state has lowest literacy rate in India?
exp: According to the census completed in 2011, Bihar has the lowest literacy percentage of any state in the country. Both males and females in Bihar have among of the lowest literacy rates in the country (males:, females: ). It reaches its greatest height in Kerala (male:, female: ). Hence the correct answer is Option D :Bihar.

subject: gk
q: "All India Muslim League" was formed at Dacca in _____ .
exp: The All-India Muslim League (AIML) was established on the 30th of December in 1906 in Dhaka, which is currently located in Bangladesh. This city was a part of British India at the time. The founders include Khwaja Salimullah, Vikar-ul-Mulk, Syed Amir Ali, Syed Nabiullah, Khan Bahadur Ghulam and Mustafa Chowdhury. Sir Sultan Muhammad Shah, also known as Aga Khan III, was the first person to hold the position of Honorary President of the League. Hence, the correct answer is "D) 1906."

subject: gk
q: In which year was India House established by Shyamji Verma?
exp: The correct answer is A. 1905. India House was established by Shyamji Krishna Varma in London in 1905. It was a student residence and a meeting place for Indian revolutionaries. Varma was a lawyer and a nationalist who had been forced to flee India after being accused of sedition. He established the India House to promote the cause of Indian independence.

subject: history
q: In the _______________ Sarojini Naidu persuaded Mahatma Gandhi to allow women to join the movement.
exp: 71 people that followed Gandhi on the 240-mile march that took place over the course of 24 days from the Sabarmati Ashram to Dandi between the 12th of March and the 6th of April 1930. Sarojini Naidu and Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay were successful in convincing Mahatma Gandhi to let women to participate in the march. Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma recently unveiled the Mission Bhumiputra Portal. Within a month, students should be able to get digital caste certificates through this service. To address land-related concerns, the state government launched Mission Basundhara in October 2021. Hence, the correct answer is "Salt Satyagraha".

subject: reasoning
q: Consider the given statement/s to be true and decide which of the given conclusions/assumptions can definitely be drawn from the given statement. Statement: Laugh and the world will laugh with you. Assumptions: I. People generally laugh. II. Laughter symbolises happiness.
o: Both I and II assumptions are implicit
Neither I nor II assumption is implicit
exp: Statement: Laugh and the world will laugh with you. This suggests that laughter is contagious or that people tend to respond to laughter positively. Evaluating the Assumptions: Assumption I: "People generally laugh." The statement does not indicate whether people generally laugh. It only suggests that if you laugh, others might laugh with you. This assumption is not necessarily true based on the given statement. Assumption II: "Laughter symbolizes happiness." The statement implies that laughter is a positive reaction, which is often associated with happiness. This assumption is reasonable and valid because laughter is generally seen as a sign of joy. Hence, Only assumption II is implicit is the correct answer.

subject: reasoning
q: Consider the given statement/s to be true and decide which of the given conclusions/assumptions can definitely be drawn from the given statement. Statement: If he works hard he will be successful in life. Conclusions: I. He is a hard worker. Conclusions: II. Hard work pays
exp: Let's analyze carefully. Statement: If he works hard, he will be successful in life. This is a conditional statement — it tells us what will happen if he works hard. It does not say whether he actually works hard or not. Conclusion I: He is a hard worker. This does not follow, because the statement never says he does work hard — only what would happen if he did. So, ❌ Conclusion I does not follow. Conclusion II: Hard work pays. This is consistent with the statement — the statement implies that working hard leads to success, i.e., hard work pays. So, ✅ Conclusion II follows. Hence, Only II follows is the correct answer.

subject: reasoning
q: In the question a statement is given, followed by two arguments, and II. You have to consider the statement to be true even if it seems to be at variance from commonly known facts. You have to decide which of the given arguments, if any, is a strong argument. Statement : Should songs be eliminated from Indian movies. Argument I: Yes, Hollywood movies are hit despite having no songs. Argument II : No, songs help increase length of the movie.
o: If only argument I is strong.
If only argument II is strong.
If both I and II are strong.
If neither I nor II is strong.
exp: In this question, according to the given statement, we have to find if any or both augments are strong. Given Statement : Should songs be eliminated from Indian movies. The success of a Hollywood movie without songs does not guarantee a hit for Bollywood movies if songs are removed. So, this argument is not strong. Similarly, The duration of a movie does not determine its success. So, this argument is not strong. So, according to the statement given neither of the argument given is strong here. Hence, the correct answer is If neither I nor II is strong.

subject: history
q: The silver coin 'tanka' was introduced by __________ .
exp: Option A: Qutubuddin Aibak → Founder of Slave dynasty, but he did not issue the silver tanka. Option B: Iltutmish → ✔ He introduced the silver tanka (standard coin) and the copper jital. Option C: Balban → Known for strong centralised rule, but not for introducing tanka. Option D: Bahram Khan → Weak ruler, no such contribution. Hence, the correct answer is "Iltutmish ".

subject: history
q: Who has built the Vijay Stambha (Tower of Victory) in Chittorgarh?
exp: The Vijay Stambha is a victory monument which is located inside the premises of Chittorgarh fort in Chittorgarh, Rajasthan. The tower was constructed by Mewar king Rana Kumbha, in 1448. This tower was built after the victory over the armies of Malwa and Gujarat led by Mahmud Khilji. Kumbha was a son of Rana Mokal of Mewar and Sobhagya Devi, daughter of Jaitmal Sankhla. Hence, the correct answer is "Rana Kumbha".

subject: history
q: ________, succeeded to the throne of Ferghana in 1494 when he was only 12 years old.
exp: Babur was the founder of the Mughal dynasty in the Indian subcontinent. Following the death of his father Umar Shaikh Mirza, Babur ascended to the throne of Ferghana at the tender age of 12 in 1494. This event marked the beginning of Babur's illustrious journey in history. In 1526, he emerged victorious over Ibrahim Lodi in the Battle of Panipat, a significant milestone in the establishment of Mughal rule in India. Babur's conquests and leadership laid the groundwork for the flourishing Mughal Empire in the centuries to come. Hence, the correct answer is "Babur."

subject: history
q: The Chola kingdom mostly ruled which region of India?
exp: The Chola dynasty governed over a large region of southern India for 400 years, involving the entirety of the present state of Tamil Nadu and nearby regions of southern Karnataka and Andhra. They built a strong navy, that helped them conquering Sri Lanka and the Maldives. They are the longest-ruling dynasties in the history of southern India. The earliest citations to this Tamil dynasty are in inscriptions from the 3rd century BCE left by Ashoka, of the Maurya Empire. Hence, the correct answer is “South”.

subject: history
q: Mattancherry Palace is located in?
exp: The Mattancherry Palace, also known as the Dutch Palace, is situated in Mattancherry, Kochi. It was built by the Portuguese and later renovated by the Dutch. The palace is renowned for its Kerala murals that depict various portraits and scenes. Additionally, it houses exhibits related to the Rajas of Kochi. The architecture reflects a blend of Portuguese, Dutch, and traditional Kerala styles. Hence, the correct answer is "Kerala."

subject: history
q: Who was the architect of Taj Mahal?
exp: Taj Mahal is located in Agra, Uttar Pradesh. Ustad Ahmad Lahaori was the architect of Taj Mahal. It is made up of white marble. It is an example of Indo-Islamic architecture. It is also included in UNESCOWorld heritage list. Taj Mahal was built by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan in the memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal. Hence, the correct answer is "Ustad Ahamad Lahouri".

subject: history
q: Jama Masjid of Delhi was built by?
exp: The Masjid-I-Jahan - Numa also called the Jama Masjid of Delhi is one of the largest mosques in India. It was built by Mughal emperor Shah Jahan and inaugurated by an imam from Bukhara, present-day Uzbekistan. The mosque was completed in 1656 AD. Jama Masjid remained the royal mosque of the emperors until the end of the Mughal period. It has three great gates, two 40 m high minarets, and four towers constructed of strips of red sandstone and white marble. Hence, the correct answer is “Shah Jahan”.

subject: history
q: Which dynasty came to power in India after the Tughlaq dynasty?
exp: The Delhi Sultanate was an Islamic kingdom that stretched over large parts of India for 320 years (1206-1526 AD). Five dynasties that ruled as a part Delhi Sultanate are as follows: Mamluk dynasty (1206-1290 AD) Khilji dynasty (1290-1320 AD) Tughlaq dynasty (1320-1414 AD) Sayyid dynasty (1414-1451 AD) Lodi dynasty (1451-1526 AD) The Sayyid dynasty was the fourth dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate. It was ruled by four Sultans from the period 1414 to 1451. Established by the then governor of Multan, Khizr Khan, in 1414 they replaced the Tughlaq dynasty. Hence, The correct answer is "The Sayyids".

subject: history
q: The Mongols under _________ invaded Transoxiana in north-east Iran in 1219.
exp: The Mongols under Genghis Khan invaded Transoxiana in northeast Iran in 1219. The Mongols under Genghis Khan invaded the Delhi Sultanate and faced their onslaught. Mongol attacks on the Delhi Sultanate increased during the reign of Alauddin Khalji and in the early years of Muhammad Tughluq's rule. Nadir Shah invaded India in 1739. He was the founder of the Afsharid dynasty. Ahmed Shah Abdali invaded India 8 times from 1748 to 1767. The third battle of Panipat was fought between Maratha & Ahmed Shah Abdali in 1761. Hence the correct answer is “Genghis Khan.”

subject: history
q: Dara Shikoh was killed in conflict with his brother ________.
exp: Dara Shikoh was killed by his younger brother Aurangzeb. The incident occurred on 30th August 1659. It took place in the battle of Samugarh. Aurangzeb was fighting against his brother Dara Shikoh for the Mughal throne. Hence, the correct answer is "Aurangzeb."

subject: history
q: Who started the construction of Nalanda (Mahavihara)?
exp: The Nalanda (Mahavihara) was established during the reign of Kumaragupta and is located near Patna, the state capital of Bihar. The Archaeological Site of Nalanda Mahavihara at Nalanda, Bihar contains the remains of a Buddhist monastic and educational center. In the 3rd century BC, the main stupa was built by Emperor Ashoka and it contains the ruins of Sariputta, one of the two chief male disciples of Gautama Buddha. Hence, the correct answer is "Kumaragupta".

subject: history
q: The Tomara Rajputs were defeated in the middle of the twelfth century by the Chauhans of_______.
exp: The Tomara was an Indian empire that ruled parts of present-day Delhi and Haryana during the 9th-12th century. Tomara Rajputs were defeated in the mid-twelfth century by the Chauhans of Ajmer. The Tomara dynasty ruled India during the 8th-12th century. Their dynasty was enlarged and ruled parts of present-day Delhi and Haryana. The capital of the dynasty was Anangpur. The last king of the dynasty was Anangpal. Anangpal handed over the throne of Delhi to his son-in-law Prithviraj Chauhan. Hence, the correct answer is “Ajmer”.

subject: history
q: Sher Khan defeated _________ at Chausa (1539) and Kanauj (1540), forcing him to flee to Iran.
exp: Sher Khan, an ethnic Pashtun, defeated Humayun at Chausa in 1539 and Kanauj in 1540. These defeats led to Humayun fleeing to Iran for refuge. Sher Khan established the Sur Dynasty but died in an accidental death in 1545. He was succeeded by his son, Islam Shah. Hence, the correct answer is "Humayun."

subject: history
q: The second Battle of Tarain was fought between_____?
exp: The second Battle of Tarain occurred in 1192. It was a significant conflict between Mohammed Ghori, the Afghan ruler, and Prithviraj Chauhan, the Rajput king. The battle took place near the town of Tarain in present-day Haryana, India. Mohammed Ghori was successful in defeating Prithviraj Chauhan in this battle. This victory paved the way for the establishment of Muslim rule in northern India. Prithviraj Chauhan was captured and later executed by Mohammed Ghori. Hence, the correct answer is "Mohammed Ghori and Prithviraj Chauhan."

subject: history
q: Buland Darwaza is located in?
exp: Buland Darwaza, also known as the "Gate of Magnificence," was constructed in 1601 A.D. by the Mughal Emperor Akbar. It was built to commemorate his victory over Gujarat. The Buland Darwaza serves as the main entrance to the palace complex at Fatehpur Sikri. Fatehpur Sikri is located approximately 43 kilometres from the city of Agra, in the state of Uttar Pradesh. Hence, the correct answer is "Uttar Pradesh."

subject: history
q: According to the categories of land mentioned in the Chola inscriptions, ________ was known as the land donated to Jaina institutions.
exp: Pallichchhandam was designated as land donated to Jaina institutions. Vellanvagai was for non-Brahmana peasant proprietors. Brahmadeya referred to tax-free land gifts to Brahmins. Shalabhoga was allocated for the maintenance of schools. Hence, the correct answer is "Pallichchhandam."

subject: history
q: Who amongst the following was the successor of Sikh Guru Har Krishan?
exp: From the late 15th century to the beginning of the 18th century, ten successive Gurus consciously channeled and acknowledged the power of the Shabad Guru. They revolutionized the spiritual, social, economic, and political life of their time. Some of them are: Guru Har Krishan Sahib (1661 to 1664) was installed as a Guru at the age of five years. Guru Teg Bahadur Sahib was his successor. Guru Angad Dev (1539 to 1552): second of the 10 gurus, invented and introduced the Gurmukhi script. Guru Amar Das Sahib (1552 to 1574): introduced the Anand Karaj marriage ceremony for the Sikhs. Guru Har Gobind Sahib (1606 to 1644): He was the son of Guru Arjan Dev. He was known as a "soldier saint” because he organized a small army and became the first Guru to take up arms to defend the faith. Guru Teg Bahadur Sahib (1665 to 1675): He established the town of Anandpur. Hence, the correct answer is “Guru Teg Bahadur”.

subject: history
q: The Red Fort in Delhi was the residence of emperors of which dynasty in the 16th century?
exp: The Mughal dynasty, under Emperor Shah Jahan, constructed the Red Fort in Delhi. Completed in 1648, the Red Fort served as the main residence of the Mughal emperors for nearly 200 years. It was designed to be the centre of Mughal power and governance in the capital city of Shahjahanabad (present- day Old Delhi). The fort's imposing red sandstone walls housed not only the royal residence but also various administrative and ceremonial buildings. Its architectural grandeur and historical significance make it one of the most iconic symbols of Mughal architecture in India. Hence, the correct answer is "Mughal."

subject: history
q: Sultan Mahmud was a ruler of_______
exp: Mahmud of Ghazni was the first independent ruler of the Ghaznavid dynasty. He was the first ruler to hold the title of Sultan. In 1018 he attacked Mathura. He sieged Gwalior in 1023. In 1025 he attacked Somnath temple and looted it 17 times. Hence, the correct answer is “Ghazni”.

subject: aptitude
q: In what ratio sugar at Rs 30/kg should be mixed with sugar at Rs 45/kg so that on selling the mixture at Rs 42/kg there is a profit of 20%?
exp: The cost price of mixed the sugar = ₹35 per kg Using Alligation; ∴ Ratio of sugars to be taken = 12 ∶ 6 = 2 ∶ 1 Hence, Option A is the correct answer.

subject: history
q: The first Europeans to come to India were
exp: The Portuguese were the first Europeans to arrive in India and the last to leave. In c. 1498 CE, Vasco da Gama of Portugal discovered a new sea route from Europe to India. In 1453, the Ottoman Turks captured Constantinople and this brought the regular trade routes under the control of the Turks. This urged the Europeans to search for new trade routes, especially by sea. Hence, the correct answer is "Portuguese".

subject: history
q: Do or Die' is associated with which of the movements in India's freedom struggle ?
exp: The slogan "Do or Die" is associated with the Quit India Movement launched by Mahatma Gandhi in 1942. Here's a more detailed explanation: Context: During World War II, Mahatma Gandhi launched the Quit India Movement (also known as the August Movement) demanding an end to British rule in India. Slogan: In his Quit India speech on August 8, 1942, at the Gowalia Tank Maidan in Bombay, Gandhi urged people to "Do or Die". Significance: The slogan "Do or Die" reflected the Indian people's determination to achieve independence from British rule at any cost. Other Movements: Dandi March: This was a civil disobedience movement led by Gandhi to protest the British salt monopoly. Non-Cooperation Movement: This was a widespread civil disobedience campaign launched by Gandhi in 1920 to boycott British institutions and products. Khilafat Movement: This movement protested against the British government's actions regarding the Ottoman Empire. Hence, the correct answer is option (D).

subject: history
q: In 1918, Mahatma Gandhi organised a satyagraha to support the peasants of the Kheda district of ______.
exp: Mahatma Gandhi started satyagraha movements in various places after arriving in India. Gandhiji started Satyagraha in the Kheda district of Gujarat in support of the peasants. The Champaran Satyagraha of 1917 was the first satyagraha movement led by Mahatma Gandhi. The following year, 1918, Gandhiji was involved in two campaigns in his home state of Gujarat. First, Gandhi JI arose in a labor dispute in Ahmedabad, demanding better working conditions for the textile mill workers. After that, he joined peasants in Kheda in demanding the state for the reduction of taxes following the failure of their harvest. Hence, the correct option is “Gujarat”.

subject: history
q: The queen with the title Didda ruled over which part of India between 980-1003?
exp: Didda was the daughter of Simharaja who was king of Lohara. Didda ruled over Kashmir from 958 CE to 1003 CE. She was married to the King of Kashmir Ksemagupta to unite the Lohara with her Kingdom of her husband. She first acted as regent for her son and became the sole monarch from 980 CE. Source of information about Didda is Rajtarangini written by Kalhana. Hence, the correct answer is “Kashmir”.

subject: history
q: In which year (in AD) was the East India Company established?
exp: The English East India Company, formally known as “The Governor and Company of Merchants of London Trading into the East Indies”, was established in 1600 AD. In 1609 AD, William Hawkins visited the court of Jahangir to seek permission to establish a factory at Surat, but he was not successful. In 1613 AD, the English established their first factory at Surat with the permission of the Mughal authorities. In 1615 AD, Sir Thomas Roe visited Jahangir’s court as an ambassador of James I and secured trade privileges for the English in India. Hence, the correct answer is “1600”.

subject: history
q: Arrest of _________ in 1930 led to angry demonstrations in the streets of Peshawar.
exp: Arrest of Abdul Ghaffar Khan in 1930 led to angry demonstrations on the streets of Peshawar. Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan led the Khudai Khitmadgar which was a group of Pashtun people committed to removing British rule through non-violence. On 23 April 1930, Ghaffar Khan was arrested for giving a speech in Utmanzai urging resistance to British rule. Abul Kalam Azad was the first Education Minister of India and was awarded Bharat Ratna in 1992 posthumously. Zakir Hussain was the first Muslim President of India and was the third President of India. Hence, the correct answer is Abdul Ghaffar Khan. Muzaffar Ahmed was a politician and was one of the founders of the communist movement in India. Hence, the correct answer is “Abdul Ghaffar Khan”.

subject: history
q: The Poona Pact was signed between Mahatma Gandhi and _____.
exp: The Poona Pact was an agreement signed on 24th September 1932. It was an understanding reached between Mahatma Gandhi and Dr. B. R. Ambedkar. The pact focused on the reservation of electoral seats for the depressed classes in British India's legislative assemblies. The signing took place at Yerwada Central Jail in Poona, where Gandhi was imprisoned at the time. The agreement aimed to ensure fair representation and upliftment of the depressed classes within the political framework. Hence, the correct answer is "B. R. Ambedkar."

subject: history
q: Lord Cornwallis is known for ____.
o: land revenue settlement of United States
exp: Lord Cornwallis took charge as the Commander-in-chief of British India and The Governor- General of Fort William Bengal. He served as the Governor-General of India from 1786 to 1793. He introduced the Permanent settlement system in Bengal and other parts of the country. Warren Hastings attacked the caste system. Sir Thomas Munro introduced the ryotwari settlement in Madras. Principle of Ryotwari Settlement: Direct collection of the land revenue by the government from each individual cultivator termed as "ryots".Hence removing the middlemen. Hence, the correct answer is “permanent revenue settlement of Bengal”.

subject: history
q: During their rule the British persuaded or forced cultivators in Assam to grow
exp: During their rule, the British forced cultivators in various parts of India to produce crops that could bring economic benefits to their trade in India. They forced farmers to produce tea in Assam wheat in Punjab sugarcane in Uttar Pradesh, cotton in Maharashtra jute in Bengal rice in Madras Though they were commercially benefitted from the same but it had a negative impact on the agricultural land and to the lives of peasants and farmers working on those lands due to very less return.It was also one of the reasons for nationalist movements in India. Hence, the correct answer is “Tea”.

subject: history
q: Who gave the slogan 'Back to the Vedas (Vedo ki aur lauto)'?
exp: Swami Dayanand Saraswati gave the slogan ‘ Back to Vedas.’ Dayanand Saraswati wanted to put society in touch with its roots so going back to vedas was the best way. Arya Samaj was founded by Swami Dayananda Saraswati in 1875. He translated the Vedas and wrote three books named Satyartha Prakash, Veda Bhasya & Veda Bhasya Bhumika. Dayanand Anglo Vedic schools were established based on his philosophy. Mission Leader Founder of Sikhism Guru Nanak Ji Ramkrishna Mission Swami Vivekananda Brahmo Samaj Raja Ram Mohan Roy Hence the correct answer is “ Dayanand Saraswati.”

subject: history
q: Who was the founder of Banaras Hindu University?
exp: Banaras Hindu University was established by the ‘B.H.U. Act 1915’ in 1916. Madan Mohan Malaviya served as the Vice-Chancellor of BHU from 1919 to 1938. He was a prominent Indian educationist and politician. Malaviya played a significant role in the Indian independence movement. His vision for BHU was to blend traditional Indian education with modern Western learning. Under his leadership, BHU became one of the premier educational institutions in India. Hence, the correct answer is "Madan Mohan Malaviya."

subject: history
q: Who was the pioneer of the Chipko movement of 1973?
exp: The Chipko Movement was started by Sunderlal Bahuguna and the movement picked up pace in 1973. The movement was begun to prevent the cutting of trees. The Chipko Movement followed the Gandhian method of nonviolence and Satyagraha. Sambhaji Bhosale was the eldest son of Shivaji, the founder of the Maratha Empire. He was the second Chhatrapati of the Maratha Empire. He ruled from 1681 to 1689. Baba Amte was an Indian social worker and activist known mainly for his work in rehabilitating and empowering people suffering from leprosy. Medha Patkar has been a central organizer and strategist for Narmada Bachao Andolan (NBA), a people's movement organized to stop the construction of a series of dams planned for India's largest westward-flowing river, the Narmada. Hence, the correct answer is “Sunderlal Bahuguna”.

subject: history
q: Which one is the correct chronological order of the following events? I. Quit India Movement II. Shimla Conference III. Poona Pact IV. Cabinet Mission
exp: Quit India movement is also known as August Kranti movement and was launched on 8th August 1942 by Mahatma Gandhi demanding an end of British Rule in the country. Shimla Conference was held in 1945 and was convened to agree on Wavell's plan for self Governance for India and to provide separate representation to communal lines. Poona pact was held on 24th September 1932 between Mahatma Gandhi and B.R. Ambedkar who accepted that the depressed class is the most discriminated section of Indian society. Cabinet Mission came in 1946 to discuss the transfer of power from the British government to Indian leaders. Hence, the correct answer is “III, I, II, IV”.

subject: history
q: Name the British General who was responsible for the Jallianwalla Bagh massacre.
exp: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre occurred on April 13, 1919, during the British colonial rule in India. Troops of the British Indian Army opened fire on unarmed civilians who had gathered in Jallianwala Bagh in Amritsar. The orders to open fire were given by Colonel Reginald Edward Harry Dyer. The incident resulted in a significant loss of life and sparked outrage across India. Dyer's actions were widely condemned, both in India and in Britain, leading to a formal inquiry known as the Hunter Commission. The massacre played a crucial role in shaping the Indian independence movement. Hence, the correct answer is "Dyer."

subject: history
q: During their rule, the British persuaded or forced cultivators in Madras to grow _________.
exp: The British monarch decided that they will use Indian villages to grow crops like wheat, rice, jute, and Tea. These crops were in demand in Britain. Britishres forces Indian farmers to grow Jute in Bengal, Tea in Assam, Sugarcane in Uttar Pradesh, cotton in Maharashtra, and Rice in Madras. Hence, the correct answer is “Rice”.

subject: history
q: Who was the founder of the Ghadar Party?
exp: The Ghadar Party was formed in 1913 in the United States and initially, it was known as the Pacific Coast Hindustan Association. The Ghadar Movement was an international political movement started by deported Indians to overthrow British rule in India. It was founded under the leadership of Lala Har Dayal, Sant Baba Wasakha Singh Dadehar, Baba Jawala Singh, Santokh Singh and Sohan Singh Bhakna as its president. Headquarter - San Francisco In 1914, after the outbreak of World War I, many members of the Ghadar party returned to Punjab to incite an armed revolution for Indian Independence. The Ghadar party was formally dissolved in 1948. Hence, the correct answer is “Lala Hardayal”.

subject: history
q: Murshid Quli Khan Alivardi Khan and Sirajuddaullah were all nawabs of ___________
exp: Murshid Quli Khan, Alivaridi Khan, and Sirajuddaullah were nawabs of Bengal. Murshid Quli Khan was the first nawab of Bengal. Alivardi Khan was a nawab of Bengal from 1740-1756. Sirajuddaullah was the last independent Nawab of Bengal. The end of his reign marked the beginning of British East India Company rule over Bengal. Hence, the correct answer is "Bengal".

subject: history
q: Which Governor General abolished the 'Sati System' in India?
exp: Lord William Bentinck was the Governor General of India who took significant steps to abolish the Sati system. He issued Regulation XVII in December 1829, which declared the practice of Sati illegal. Sati, the practice where a widow was compelled to self-immolate on her husband's funeral pyre, was prevalent in some parts of India. The regulation not only banned the practice but also made it punishable by law. Bentinck's decision was influenced by both humanitarian considerations and pressures from reformist groups. Hence, the correct answer is "Lord William Bentinck."

subject: history
q: Who was the first Viceroy of India?
exp: Under the Government of India Act of 1858, the power was transferred from the East India Company to the British Crown. The Governor General was given the title of Viceroy. Lord Canning was the first Viceroy of India. His tenure was from 1858-1862. Lord Mountbatten was the last Viceroy of India. Lord Curzon is associated with the Partition of Bengal. Lord Wavell was the second last Viceroy and was succeeded by Lord Mountbatten. Hence, the correct answer is “Lord Canning”.

subject: history
q: Which of the following was a leader of the Hindustan Socialist Republican Army founded in 1928?
exp: Hindustan Socialist Republican Army was established in 1928 at Feroz Shah Kotla in New Delhi. Leaders associated with this army were Sukhdev Thapar, Bhagat Singh, Chandrashekhar Azad, etc. Its main leader was Chandrashekhar Azad. This party was initially named as Hindustan Republican Association which was formed by Ram Prasad Bismil in 1923 at Allahabad. Most famous incident by HSRA was the Kakori conspiracy which occurred on 9th August 1925 in which party members looted a train carrying government money near Lucknow. Hence, the correct answer is “Chandra Shekhar Azad”.

subject: history
q: Who raised the slogan "Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it"?
exp: Bal Gangadhar Tilak gave the popular slogan, "Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it" in the Bombay State Political Conference that was held in 1916. Bal Gangadhar Tilak was popularly known as Lokmanya Tilak. He formed a prominent organization named Deccan Education Society that promotes modern learning. He established Fergusson College at Pune . He, along with Annie Besant, played a remarkable role during the Home Rule Movement (1916-18). Mahratta & Kesari were the two newspapers started by Bal Gangadhar Tilak. Hence, the correct answer is "Bal Gangadhar Tilak".

subject: history
q: Gol Gumbaz was designed by?
exp: The Gol Gumbaz, also called Gol Gumbadh ,was constructed by Adil Shah II. It was designed by an architect Yaqut of Dabul. It is located in Bijapur and in Bijapur it is known as the "Whispering Gallery". The architectural style of Gumbaz is Deccan Indo- Islamic. Hence, the correct answer is “Yaqut of Dabul”.

subject: history
q: Who was the first Governor General of Bengal?
exp: The first governor-general in India (of Bengal) was Warren Hastings in 1773. He began his career as a writer (clerk) in the East India Company at Calcutta in 1750. Warren Hastings established the revenue board in 1772, aiming for better financial administration. He abolished the dual system of governance, streamlining the administrative structure. In partnership with William Jones, he founded the Asiatic Society of Bengal in 1784 in Calcutta, promoting learning and research. Hastings laid the groundwork for the civil service, which was later reformed and modernized by Lord Cornwallis. Hence, the correct answer is "Warren Hastings".

subject: history
q: Which act ended the "Trade Monopoly" of the East India Company?
exp: The Regulating Act of 1773 officially, the East India Company Act 1772 was an Act of the Parliament of Great Britain that proposed to refurbish the management of the East India Company's rule in India. But the Act did not prove to be a long-term solution to concerns over the company's affairs. So Pitt's India Act was therefore subsequently passed in 1784 as a more radical reform. The East India Company's monopoly over trade with China and tea with India was protected by the Charter Act of 1813, which also eliminated the company's monopoly on trade in India. The East India Company's business was given an additional 20 years of rule. The act gave permission to those who liked to visit India to expand their moral and religious beliefs. It monitored the company's commercial benefits and territorial revenues. It was hoped that it would keep its commercial and territorial accounts independent. The Charter Act of 1833 also called the Saint Helena Act of 1833 or the Government of India Act of 1833. This act was the first act in which natives of India were free to participate in a democratic system of government. Hence, the correct answer is “The Charter Act of 1813”.

subject: history
q: Who led the Bardoli Satyagraha movement?
exp: Bardoli Satyagraha occurred in 1928 in Gujarat during the British Raj. Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel led the movement. The movement aimed to reduce taxes due to the year's calamities. Patel instructed Bardoli farmers to refuse tax payment and remain non-violent. The struggle sought not only tax cancellation but also the return of seized property. Hence, the correct answer is "Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel."

subject: english
q: In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct speech. He said, "Why did you give up your job?"
o: He asked her why she had given up her job.
He asked her why you gave up the job.
He demand to know why she gave up job.
He requested her why she gave up the job.
exp: The Correct Answer: Option A - He asked her why she had given up her job. This is an interrogative sentence (wh- question) and it’s being reported in indirect speech, so the structure will change as follows: Rules to apply: 1. Said → changes to asked (since it’s a question). 2. "Why did you give up..." → backshift the verb to "had given up" (past simple → past perfect). 3. "your" changes based on the subject – here, the subject is likely "her". Other Options: B) Incorrect: "you gave up" is not backshifted, and "you" is not changed to "she". C) Incorrect: "demand" is too strong and grammatically incorrect in structure. D) Incorrect: "requested" is not used for questions, and the verb tense isn't shifted.

subject: english
q: In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best express the same sentence in Indirect/Direct speech. He said that when he was a boy he could stay up as long as he liked.
o: He said,"When I had been a boy I could stay up as long as I liked."
He told, "When I was a boy I could stay up as long as I liked."
He said,"When I was a boy I could stay up as long as I liked."
He said,"When I am a boy I can stay up as long as I like."
exp: The Correct Answer: Option C — He said,"When I was a boy I could stay up as long as I liked." Explanation: When converting indirect speech to direct speech, we need to make several changes: The reporting verb "said" remains the same. We remove the conjunction "that" and add quotation marks around the direct speech. Pronouns change according to the original speaker's perspective: — "he" (third person) changes back to "I" (first person, as the speaker is referring to himself) For this sentence, the tenses remain the same because: — "was" (simple past) remains "was" in direct speech as it refers to a specific past time — "could" (past modal) remains "could" as it's already appropriate for the past time reference — "liked" (simple past) remains "liked" as it maintains the past reference The time clause "when I was a boy" correctly establishes the past time frame, so no further tense changes are needed. IN HINGLISH: Indirect speech को direct speech में बदलते समय हमें कुछ जरूरी बदलाव करने होते हैं: Reporting verb "said" में कोई tense change नहीं किया जाता, यह same रहता है। "That" को हटा दिया जाता है और direct speech को quotation marks में लिखा जाता है। Pronouns को original speaker की दृष्टि से बदला जाता है: — "he" (third person) वापस "I" (first person) बन जाता है क्योंकि वक्ताा खुद के बारे में बात कर रहा है। इस sentence में tense change नहीं होता क्योंकि original reference already past time है और context clear है। For this sentence: "was" (simple past) → remains "was" — क्योंकि यह एक specific past time बताता है। "could" (past modal) → remains "could" — यह पहले से ही past context के लिए सही है। "liked" (simple past) → remains "liked" — past reference को maintain करता है, इसलिए change नहीं होगा। | | SSC Time clause “when I was a boy” पहले ही past time frame को स्पष्ट कर देता है, इसलिए tense में और कोई बदलाव आवश्यक नहीं है।

subject: english
q: In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best express the same sentence in Indirect/Direct speech. He said, "How can a Zebra talk?"
o: He wondered how a Zebra talks.
He asked how a Zebra could talk.
He was amazed how a Zebra can talk.
exp: Correct Answer: Option C — He asked how a Zebra could talk. Explanation: The given sentence is an interrogative sentence (question form). "How can a Zebra talk?" When converting an interrogative sentence into indirect speech: “said” changes to asked (or inquired). The question form changes into a statement form (no question mark). The auxiliary verb shifts according to tense rule: can → could (because reporting verb “said” is in past tense). The word order becomes: how + subject + verb So the correct indirect form is: He asked how a Zebra could talk.

subject: english
q: In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct speech. "Good-bye! Dear friend," said the patriot, "we will meet again."
o: The patriot said good-bye to his dear friend and said that they will meet again.
The patriot bade his friend good-bye and said that they must meet again.
Bidding his dear friend good-bye, the patriot said that they would meet again.
The patriot said good-bye to his friend and said that they are sure to meet again.
exp: The correct alternative to express the given sentence in Indirect speech is: "Bidding his dear friend good-bye, the patriot said that they would meet again." This option accurately transforms the direct speech into indirect speech while maintaining the correct tense changes and attributions. The phrase "bidding his dear friend good-bye" replaces the original statement "Good-bye! Dear friend," as a suitable introduction to the reported speech. The change in tense from "will" to "would" is also applied correctly to the reported speech.

subject: english
q: In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct speech. I said to the old man, "Don't sit on that chair; it is broken."
o: I cautioned the old man against sitting on that chair as it was broken.
I cautioned the old man against sitting on that chair, it will be broken.
I requested the old man not to sit on that chair because it is broken.
I asked the old man not to sit on the chair as it is broken.
exp: The Correct Answer: Option A — I cautioned the old man against sitting on that chair as it was broken. Explanation: To convert direct speech into indirect speech, we follow several rules based on the type of sentence and the verbs used: Sentence Type: The original sentence is an imperative sentence containing a negative command — "Don't sit on that chair..." Reporting Verb: For negative commands or warnings, appropriate reporting verbs include warned, cautioned, or advised instead of "told" or "asked". Since the sentence implies warning due to a broken chair, "cautioned" is the most appropriate verb. Change in Structure: Imperative sentences in indirect speech often use the gerund (-ing form) when followed by "against". "Don't sit" changes to "against sitting". Tense Consistency: The original has "it is broken". As the reporting verb "said" is in the past, shift the tense to past: "is" → "was". Pronouns and Reference Words: "That chair" remains the same in indirect speech.

subject: english
q: In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct speech. He said, "How I wish they would come!"
o: He exclaimed that he wished they would come.
He exclaimed hopefully that they would come.
He exclaimed that he would wish them to come.
He exclaimed how he wished they would come.
exp: The correct answer is Option A. Direct Speech: "He said, 'How I wish they would come!'" Exclamatory Sentence: The expression "How I wish..." conveys a strong desire or hope. Reporting Verb Change: In indirect speech, "said" is changed to "exclaimed" to convey the emotion expressed in the sentence. Conjunction: The exclamatory expression is converted into a statement using "that". Meaning Preserved: Option A correctly conveys the speaker's wish without altering the intended meaning. Therefore, the correct answer is Option A. Correct Sentence: "He exclaimed that he wished they would come." Option B: "He exclaimed hopefully that they would come." Incorrect because it changes the original structure and does not convey the explicit wish expressed by the speaker. Option C: "He exclaimed that he would wish them to come." Incorrect because the construction "would wish" is unnatural and alters the meaning. Option D: "He exclaimed how he wished they would come." Incorrect because the conjunction "how" is unnecessary in indirect narration and makes the sentence awkward.

subject: english
q: In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct speech. "Why don't you see a doctor?" said Mrs. Lal to Nina.
o: Mrs. Lal asked Nina why she could't see a doctor.
Mis. Lal demanded why Nina did't see her doctor.
Mrs. Lal advised Nina to see a doctor.
Mrs. Lal advised that Nina to see her doctor.
exp: The Correct Answer: Option A — Mrs. Lal asked Nina why she couldn't see a doctor. Explanation: When converting direct speech to indirect speech for questions in the form of "Why don't you...?", we need to make several changes: The reporting verb "said" changes to "asked" since this is a question. For wh-questions, we use the question word "why" directly without adding "that." The sentence structure changes from interrogative to declarative word order: "why she couldn't see" instead of "why don't you see." Pronouns change according to the new perspective: "you" (the listener, Nina) changes to "she" The negative form changes: "don't you see" changes to "she couldn't see" The contraction "don't" in present tense becomes "couldn't" (could not) in past tense with backshift We remove the quotation marks and question mark. In Hinglish: "Why don't you...?" format वाले direct speech को indirect speech में बदलते समय (जब question हो) हमें कुछ बदलाव करने पड़ते हैं: Reporting verb "said" को "asked" में बदला जाता है क्योंकि यह question है। Wh-questions के लिए question word "why" directly use किया जाता है बिना "that" add किए। Sentence structure interrogative से declarative word order में बदलता है: "why she couldn't see" न कि "why don't you see." Pronouns change according to the new perspective: — "I" (the speaker) changes to "she" — "you" (the listener) changes to "we" The tense shifts backward (backshift): — Future continuous "will be making" changes to conditional continuous "would be making" — Simple present "wish" changes to simple past "wished" Time expressions change: — "now" changes to "then" For the question part, we use the question word "what" directly without "that," maintaining the meaning of the inquiry.

q: Rajan spent 10% of his salary on rent. He spent 20% of the remaining part of the salary on transport. After which he spent 40% of the balance of the salary on food. exp: Let, the monthly salary of Rajan be Rs. 100x. Then, amount spent on rent = (100x) × 10% = Rs. 10x Remaining salary = 100x – 10x = Rs. 90x Amount spent on transport = (90x) × 20% = Rs. 18x Remaining salary = 90x – 18x = Rs. 72x Amount spent on Food = (72x) × 40% = Rs. 28.8x Remaining salary = 72x – 28.8x = Rs. 43.2x Amount spent on various bills = (43.2x) × 80% = Rs. 34.56x Remaining (deposited in the bank and kept for petty expenditure) = 5000 + 1480 ⇒ 43.2x – 34.56x = 6480 ⇒ 8.64x = 6480 ⇒ x = 6480/8.64 = 750 Therefore, salary of Ranjan = 750 × 100 = Rs. 75000 Hence, Option A is the correct answer.

q: Which type of tax acts as an automatic stabiliser in the economy?

When the economy contracts, people's incomes decrease, and so does the amount of tax revenue collected. Hence the correct answer is "D): Proportional income tax."

exp: Greenland is officially the world’s largest island that is not a continent. Home to 56,000 people, Greenland has its extensive local government, but it is also part of the Realm of Denmark. Greenland was a Danish colony until 1953 when it was redefined as a district of Denmark. In addition to its local government, Greenland has two representatives in the Danish Parliament, the Folketing. Hence, the correct answer is 'Greenland'.

subject: geography
q: The country which tops in the production of cocoa is __________ .
exp: Ivory Coast (Côte d'Ivoire) is the largest producer of cocoa in the world. It contributes around 40% of global cocoa production. Ghana is the second-largest producer. Brazil and Nigeria also produce cocoa, but on a smaller scale compared to Ivory Coast. Hence, the correct answer is "Ivory Coast".

subject: geography
q: Sea water is saltier than rain water because
o: The air around the sea is saltish
Rivers wash away salts from earth and pour them into the sea
Sea beds have salt producing mines
exp: Rainwater is pure but when it flows as rivers, it dissolves salts and minerals from rocks and soil. These dissolved salts are carried by rivers into the sea continuously over millions of years. Since water evaporates from the sea but salt does not, the salt concentration keeps increasing. Hence, the correct answer is "Rivers wash away salts from earth and pour them into the sea."

subject: geography
q: Bhutan does not share its border with which Indian state?
exp: Bhutan shares its border with four Indian states like Arunachal Pradesh, West Bengal, Sikkim, and Assam. The Indo-Bhutan border extends to 699 km. The Indo-Bhutan border was established by the Treaty of Sinchula on November 11, 1865. Only land access to Bhutan is through the border between these two countries in the district of Jaigaon, and Alipurduar in West Bengal. Capital of Bhutan in Thimphu. Hence, the correct answer is “Meghalaya”.

subject: geography
q: In April 2017, diplomatic ties were re- established after 37 years between Cuba and________.
exp: Cuba and Morocco in the third week of April 2017 signed a contract to re- establish diplomatic relations after a gap of 37 years. The statement was made by the Cuban Foreign Ministry. Havana, Spanish La Habana, city, capital, major port, and leading commercial center of Cuba, and the Cuban Convertible Peso is the currency of Cuba. It is a country located in the Greater Antilles. Morocco is a Northern African country and is located in the extreme northwest of Africa on the edge of continental Europe. The currency in Morocco is the Moroccan dirham and Rabat is the capital city. Hence, the correct answer is “ Morocco”.

subject: geography
q: Which among the following country is not a part of Scandinavia?
exp: Scandinavia is a subregion in Northern Europe, That has strong historical, cultural, and linguistic ties between its constituent peoples. In general there are 3 main Scandinavian countries. These countries are Norway, Sweden, and Denmark. Term Scandinavia comes from a region in southern Sweden known as Scania. Term ‘Norden’ refers to five countries: Sweden, Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway, and Faroe island. Hence, the correct answer is “Finland”.

subject: geography
q: Masai is a tribe of which of the following country?
exp: Masai are tribes of Northern and Central Kenya and Northern Tanzania. They are a nomadic and pastoralist tribe. Their origin is in the lower Nile valley north of Lake Turkana. Their beadwork culture signifies their beauty, tradition, strength, and social status. They believe in the ‘Enkai’ God. They speak the Massai language. Tribes of Germany are Franks, Angles, Saxons, Alamanni, etc. Tribes of Australia are Koori, Murri, Nunga, and Noongar. Tribes of India are Gond, Khond, Sahariya etc. Hence the correct answer is “Kenya”.
